Let $T(n)$ be a function defined on the natural numbers such that $T(n) = n - 3$ if $n$ is divisible by 3 and $T(n) = n + 1$ otherwise. For $k \in \mathbb{N}$, let $c_k$ denote the number of elements in the set $\{n: T^k(n) = 1\}$. Calculate the value of $c_6$.

Consider a function \( f(x) \) that is continuously differentiable on \([0, \infty)\), nonnegative, and monotone nonincreasing. Let \( S \) be the surface area of the surface of revolution formed by rotating the curve \( y = f(x) \) about the \( x \)-axis. If \( \int_0^{\infty} f(x) \, dx = 10 \), find the value of \( \int_0^{\infty} \sqrt{1 + (f'(x))^2} f(x) \, dx \).

Let \(ABC\) be a triangle with incenter \(I\) and circumcenter \(O\). Let \(\Gamma_A\), \(\Gamma_B\), and \(\Gamma_C\) be circles with radius \(p\) and centers \(A'\), \(B'\), and \(C'\) respectively, such that the legs of \(\angle BAC\) are tangents to \(\Gamma_A\), the legs of \(\angle ABC\) are tangents to \(\Gamma_B\), and the legs of \(\angle ACB\) are tangents to \(\Gamma_C\). A circle \(\Gamma\) touches each of the circles \(\Gamma_A\), \(\Gamma_B\), and \(\Gamma_C\) in exactly one point, with all three circles either inside or outside of \(\Gamma\). Let \(O'\) be the center of \(\Gamma\). If \(IO = 10\) and \(p = 3\), find the length of \(O'I\).
What is the residue of $15^{1234}$, modulo 19?
Calculate $52143_5 - 4310_8$ in base 10.

Let \( A \) be a matrix in \( GL_3(\mathbb{R}) \) and let \( b_1 = 3, b_2 = 4, b_3 = 5 \) be strictly positive real numbers such that \( b_1 \cdot b_2 \cdot b_3 > \det(A) \). Find the smallest possible value of \( \det(A) \) such that there exists a non-zero vector \( X = (x_1, x_2, x_3) \in \mathbb{Z}^3 \) for which the absolute value of the \( i \)-th coordinate of \( AX \) is less than \( b_i \) for all \( i \in \{1, 2, 3\} \).

Let \(\mathbb{N}\) be the set of all positive integers. Let \(f, g: \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}\) be functions such that \(f\) is onto and \(g\) is one-to-one, and \(f(n) \geq g(n)\) for all positive integers \(n\). Define \(h(n) = f(n) - g(n)\). Find the sum of all possible values of \(h(1) + h(2) + \cdots + h(10)\).

A train travelled from point A to point B at 160 km/h. On its way back, the train travelled at 120 km/h and therefore the trip back lasted one hour longer. What is the distance (in km) between point A and point B?
If $m$ and $n$ are odd integers, how many terms in the expansion of $(m+n)^8$ are odd?
A farmer had 171 tomatoes in his garden. If he picked 134 of them yesterday and 30 today.. How many will he have left after today?
What is the 2009th term of the sequence consisting of positive integers (in order) with the property that the sum of their digits is divisible by 4?

Given \(a, b, c > 0\) and the conditions \(a^2 + b^2 \leq \sqrt[3]{2}\), \(b^2 + c^2 \leq \sqrt[3]{2}\), and \(c^2 + a^2 \leq \sqrt[3]{2}\), find the minimum value of the expression

\[ 2(a + b + c) + \left(\frac{1}{ab} + \frac{1}{bc} + \frac{1}{ca}\right) - \left(\frac{2}{a^2 + b^2} + \frac{2}{b^2 + c^2} + \frac{2}{c^2 + a^2}\right) - \sqrt{2} \left(\sqrt{a^2 + b^2} + \sqrt{b^2 + c^2} + \sqrt{c^2 + a^2}\right). \]

The United States flag has 50 stars, one for every state in the union, and 13 stripes, which represent the original 13 colonies. Pete, inspired by history, decided to make his own flag. He used circles, to represent how many scoops of ice cream he can consume in one sitting, squares, to represent the number of brownies he has hidden beneath his bed, and triangles, to represent the number of cookies he can stack on one plate. 

For circles, he used 3 less than half the number of stars on the US flag, for squares, he used six more than twice the number of stripes on the US flag, and for triangles, he used the difference between the number of stars and stripes on the US flag, multiplied by two. 

What is the combined total number of circles, squares, and triangles on Pete's flag?
Let $S$ be a subset of $\{1, 2, 3, \ldots, 1000\}$ such that no two members of $S$ differ by $3$ or $5$. What is the largest number of elements $S$ can have?

What is the median and the mode number of moons per celestial body? Consider the following data and include Ceres and Eris in the analysis.

\begin{tabular}{c|c}
Celestial Body & $\#$ of Moons\\
\hline
Mercury & 0\\
Venus & 0\\
Earth & 1\\
Mars & 2\\
Jupiter & 18\\
Saturn & 25\\
Uranus & 15\\
Neptune & 2\\
Pluto & 5\\
Ceres & 0\\
Eris & 1\\
\end{tabular}
How many positive integers $N$ less than $2000$ are there such that the equation $x^{\lfloor x\rfloor} = N$ has a solution for $x$?

Let \( P(x) \in \mathbb{R}[x] \) be a polynomial of degree \( n \). Find the smallest possible degree of a polynomial \( Q(x) \in \mathbb{R}[x] \) such that \( P(x)Q(x) \) is a polynomial in \( x^{2001} \).
Given that \(abc = 1\), find the minimum value of the expression \(\frac{8(a^3 + b^3 + c^3)}{(a^2 + bc)(b^2 + ac)(c^2 + ab)}\).

Let \( f \) and \( g \) be two continuous and bijective functions defined from \( \mathbb{R} \) to \( \mathbb{R} \) such that 
\[ f(g^{-1}(x)) + g(f^{-1}(x)) = 2x \]
for all real numbers \( x \). Additionally, there exists a real number \( c \) such that \( f(c) = g(c) \). If \( f(1) = 3 \) and \( g(1) = 3 \), find the value of \( f(2) + g(2) \).

Bobby had 22 pieces of candy. He ate some pieces and then shared half of the amount he ate with his friend. After that, he ate 5 more pieces. If he still has 8 pieces of candy left, how many pieces of candy had he eaten at the start before sharing with his friend?
Expand the product $(5x + 3y + 2)(2x + 5y + 3)$ and determine the sum of the coefficients of the terms which contain a nonzero power of $y$.
Xander read 20% of his book in one hour. The next night he read another 20% of the book. On the third night, he read 30% of his book. He has 150 pages left to read. How many pages are in the book?

Admission tickets to a football game were some cents for adults and 25 cents for children. Receipts for the day showed that 280 persons attended and 140 dollars was collected. If 200 adults attended, how much was the cost of an adult ticket?
Compute $(-81)\div (-27)$.
What is the result of the operation 40 + 5 * 12 / ( 180 / some number ) if the answer is 41?

Let \( \Gamma \) be a circle passing through the vertex \( A \) of \( \triangle ABC \) and intersecting segments \( AC \) and \( AB \) at points \( F \) and \( E \), respectively. Let \( P \) be the intersection of \( \Gamma \) and the circumcircle of \( \triangle ABC \) (with \( P \neq A \)). If the reflection of \( P \) in line \( EF \) lies on \( BC \), find the ratio of the power of point \( O \) (the circumcenter of \( \triangle ABC \)) with respect to \( \Gamma \) to the power of point \( O \) with respect to the circumcircle of \( \triangle ABC \).

Suppose that \( p, q, r, s, t, u, v, w \) are nonnegative real numbers, not all equal to zero. Calculate the minimum value of the expression
\[
\frac{88\sqrt{pqrstuvw}}{113(p^{3}+q^{3}+r^{3}+s^{3}+t^{3}+u^{3}+v^{3}+w^{3})} - \left( \sum_{\text{cyclic}} \frac{p}{7} - \sqrt[3]{\sum_{\text{cyclic}} \frac{p^{3}}{7}} \right).
\]

Let \( P \) be any point inside \( \triangle ABC \). Denote by \( H_C \) and \( H_B \) the orthocenters of \( \triangle PAB \) and \( \triangle PAC \) respectively. The line \( PA \) intersects the circumcircle of \( \triangle BPC \) again at the point \( Q \). The point \( H \) is the projection of \( Q \) onto the line \( BC \). Calculate the measure of the angle \( \angle AH_BH_C \) in degrees.

(1) Find the coefficient of $x^3$ in the expansion of $(\frac{1}{2} - x)^5$ and the sum of all coefficients in the expansion.
(2) From the numbers 0, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, select any 4 to form a 4-digit number without repeating digits. Find the number of 4-digit numbers that meet the condition.

In space, there are 9 points where any 4 points are not coplanar. Connect several line segments among these 9 points such that no tetrahedron exists in the graph. What is the maximum number of triangles in the graph? $\qquad$ .
Two sides of a triangle measure 7 cm and 10 cm. What is the greatest integer number of centimeters that could be the third side of this triangle?
Excluding stoppages, the speed of a train is 54 kmph, and including stoppages, it is 36 kmph. How many minutes does the train stop per hour?

The roof of an apartment building is rectangular and its length is 4 times longer than its width. If the area of the roof is 900 square feet, what is the difference between the length and the width of the roof?
what number must be added to 6 , 16 and 8 to get an average of 13 ?
Let \( R \) be a ring with unity, and let \( a \) be an element in \( R \) such that \( a^2 = a \). Calculate the value of \( (1 - a)^{-1} \) in terms of \( a \).
Let \( A, B \in M_{3}(\mathbb{Z}) \) such that \( (AB)^2 - AB = (BA)^2 - BA \) and \( \det(AB - BA) = 1 \). Calculate the value of \( \det((AB)^3 - (BA)^3) \).
Find the average of all the numbers between 40 and a certain number which are divisible by 3. The average is 60. What is the ending number?
Calculate how many zeros are present at the end of the number obtained by expanding $50!$ (i.e., $50 \cdot 49 \cdot 48 \cdots 3 \cdot 2 \cdot 1$).
A class has 30 students with an average height of 140 cm. There are 18 boys in the class, and the average height of the boys is 144 cm. What is the average height of the girls, in cm?

Given a natural sequence $\{a_n\}$ such that
\[
(a_{2n} + a_{2n+1} + 1)(a_{2n+1} - a_{2n} - 1) = 3(1 + 2a_n)
\]
and
\[
a_{2n} \geq a_n \quad \text{for all } n \in \mathbb{N},
\]
find all $n \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $a_n \leq 2009$.
If xy = 1, then ( some number ^ ( x + y ) ^ 2 ) / ( some number ^ ( x - y ) ^ 2 ) equals 625. What is the value of the base number?

Consider a set of 91 nonzero vectors in the plane. Let $S$ be the sum of any 19 of these vectors, and let $T$ be the sum of the remaining 72 vectors. Determine the number of distinct possible values of the dot product $S \cdot T$.

A convex polyhedron has $9$ vertices, one of which is $A$. Parallel translations that send $A$ into each of the other vertices form $8$ equal polyhedra. Let $N$ be the number of pairs of these $8$ polyhedra that have an inner point in intersection. Calculate the minimum possible value of $N$.
What is the first year after 2010 for which the sum of the digits is 10?
Consider the sequence defined by \(a_n = \sum_{k=0}^{n} (-1)^k \binom{n}{k}^\alpha\) for all \(\alpha \in (0,1)\). Calculate the value of \(\alpha\) for which \(|a_{100}|\) is minimized.

How many four-digit parity-monotonic integers are there? An integer is called parity-monotonic if its decimal representation $a_{1}a_{2}a_{3}\cdots a_{k}$ satisfies $a_{i} < a_{i+1}$ if $a_{i}$ is odd, and $a_{i} > a_{i+1}$ if $a_{i}$ is even.
Tiffany had 6 pages of math homework and 4 pages of reading homework. If each page had 3 problems on it, how many problems did she have to complete total?
Malcolm brushes his teeth for some minutes after breakfast, lunch, and dinner. After 30 days, he spends 3 hours brushing his teeth. How many minutes does he brush his teeth after each meal?

Let \(a, b, c, d\) be real numbers. Calculate the minimum value of the expression
\[
(a^2+1)(b^2+1)(c^2+1)(d^2+1) - (a+b+c+d)^2 - \frac{8}{3}(ab+ac+ad+bc+bd+cd-6).
\]
Given vectors $\overrightarrow{a}=(x,4,3)$ and $\overrightarrow{b}=(3,2,z)$ that are parallel, find the value of $xz$.

In triangle $\Delta ABC$ with $\Delta DEF$ as the medial triangle, let $AD \cap \odot (ABE) = T$. Let $\odot (BFC) \cap \odot (ABE) = L$. Let $LT \cap \odot (BFC) = N$. If $TF = 5$, calculate the length of $TN$.
When the greatest common divisor and least common multiple of two integers are multiplied, the product is 360. How many different values could be the greatest common divisor of these two integers?
Given the function $f(x) = x^2 + |x - 2|$, find the value of $f(1)$.

Find the function \( f: \mathbb{R}_{0}^{+} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^{+} \) that satisfies the following inequality for all positive real numbers \( a, b, c \):

\[
\sum_{\text{cyc}} \frac{\sqrt{ab} (\sqrt{a^2 + \lambda bc} + \sqrt{b^2 + \lambda ca})}{\sqrt{ab} + \lambda c} \leq f(\lambda) \sum_{\text{cyc}} a
\]

A positive integer  $N$  is *apt* if for each integer  $0 < k < 1009$ , there exists exactly one divisor of  $N$  with a remainder of  $k$  when divided by  $1009$ . For a prime  $p$ , suppose there exists an *apt* positive integer  $N$  where  $\tfrac Np$  is an integer but  $\tfrac N{p^2}$  is not. Find the number of possible remainders when  $p$  is divided by  $1009$ .

*Proposed by Evan Chang*

A circle is tangent to two adjacent sides \(AB\) and \(AD\) of square \(ABCD\) and cuts off a segment of length 4 cm from vertices \(B\) and \(D\) at the points of tangency. On the other two sides, the circle intersects cutting off segments from the vertices of lengths 2 cm and 1 cm, respectively. Find the radius of the circle.

A Burmese python that was 1.4 meters long swallowed a 50-centimeter alligator.  After one week, the alligator was completely digested.  If this snake continues to eat 50-centimeter-long alligators at a constant rate of one alligator per week, what is the maximum number of alligators that the snake can eat in 616 days?
The third and fourth terms of a geometric sequence are 36 and 54, respectively. What is the first term of the sequence?

Let \( H \) be the orthocenter of triangle \( ABC \). Let the circle passing through points \( A, B, H \) have center \( R \) and intersect segment \( BC \) at point \( D \) (\( D \ne B \)). Let \( P \) be the intersection point of line \( DH \) with segment \( AC \). Let \( Q \) be the circumcenter of triangle \( ADP \). If \( \angle BDR = 120^\circ \), find the measure of \( \angle BQR \) in degrees.

Let 
\[ x^6 - x^3 - x^2 - 1 = q_1(x) q_2(x) \dotsm q_m(x), \]
where each non-constant polynomial $q_i(x)$ is monic with integer coefficients, and cannot be factored further over the integers. Compute $q_1(2) + q_2(2) + \dots + q_m(2)$.
What is the coefficient of $x^5$ in the expansion of $$(x + 3\sqrt{2})^9?$$
Let $f:\mathbb{R}\to \mathbb{R}^+$ be a continuous function such that $|f(x)| \to 0$ as $|x| \to \infty$. Define $I(a) = \int_{-a}^{a} f(x)\sin(x) \, dx$. Calculate $\lim_{a \to \infty} I(a)$.

Consider the sequence \( x_n = 1 + \frac{1}{6} + \cdots + \frac{1}{5n+1} \). Given that \( |x_n - x_m| \leq \frac{n-(m+1)}{5m+6} \) for all \( n \geq m \), find the smallest integer \( N \) such that \( |x_n - x_m| < \frac{1}{1000} \) for all \( n, m \geq N \).

A frog pond has five frogs living in it. Some frogs laid eggs, and now there are three times as many tadpoles growing into more frogs as there are frogs. Two-thirds of the tadpoles will survive to maturity as frogs. The pond can only sustain eight frogs. How many frogs will have to find a new pond when the tadpoles grow up?
The average age of the four Turner children is 9 years. The three younger children are ages 6 years, 8 years, and 11 years. How many years old is the oldest Turner child?

The Big Eighteen Basketball Conference has three divisions, with six teams in each division. Each team plays each of the other teams in its own division three times and every team in the other divisions twice. How many conference games are scheduled?

In a triangle \(ABC\) with sides \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\), the inequality \( \cos B + \cos C \ge 1 \) holds. Find the minimum value of \( \frac{1}{b} + \frac{1}{c} - \frac{1}{a-b+c} - \frac{1}{a+b-c} \).
A train that is 320 meters long is running at a speed of 45 km/hour. It takes 36.8 seconds to pass a bridge of a certain length. What is the length of the bridge?

Let  $ABC$  be a triangle, not right-angled, with positive integer angle measures (in degrees) and circumcenter  $O$ . Say that a triangle  $ABC$  is *good* if the following three conditions hold:

(a) There exists a point  $P\neq A$  on side  $AB$  such that the circumcircle of  $\triangle POA$  is tangent to  $BO$ .
(b) There exists a point  $Q\neq A$  on side  $AC$  such that the circumcircle of  $\triangle QOA$  is tangent to  $CO$ .
(c) The perimeter of  $\triangle APQ$  is at least  $AB+AC$ .

Determine the number of ordered triples  $(\angle A, \angle B,\angle C)$  for which  $\triangle ABC$  is good.

*Proposed by Vincent Huang*
Set W consists of all the prime numbers between a certain number and 25. The range of set W is 12. What is the lower limit of the range for set W?
If $f(x) = (2x + a)^2$, and $f'(2) = 20$, then $a = \boxed{1}$.

According to legend, the poet Li Bai from the Tang Dynasty went to buy wine, singing as he walked down the street. Each time he passed a store, the amount of his wine doubled, and each time he saw a flower, he drank 2 cups. After encountering four stores and flowers in total, he still had 2 cups of wine left at the end. How many cups of wine did he originally have?
If the consecutive integers from $100$ to $1$ were written as $$1009998979695...,$$ what would be the $150^{\text{th}}$ digit to be written?

Let $
g(n) =
\begin{cases}
n^2+3 & \text{if }n\text{ is odd} \\
\dfrac{n}{2} & \text{if }n\text{ is even}
\end{cases}.
$

For how many integers $n$ from 1 to 100, inclusive, does $g ( g (\dotsb g (n) \dotsb )) = 3$ for some number of applications of $g$?

Solve the quadratic equation $4x^2 - 24x - 96 = 0$ using the method of completing the square. During this process, you will come up with an equivalent equation $(x + q)^2 = t$, where $q$ and $t$ are constants.
What is $t$?

Bob grew corn in his garden and is ready to harvest it. He has 7 rows of corn with varying yields. The first row has 82 corn stalks, with about every 8 stalks producing a bushel of corn. The second row has 94 corn stalks, with about every 9 stalks producing a bushel of corn. The third row has 78 corn stalks, with about every 7 stalks producing a bushel of corn. The fourth row has 96 corn stalks, with about every 12 stalks producing a bushel of corn. The fifth row has 85 corn stalks, with about every 10 stalks producing a bushel of corn. The sixth row has 91 corn stalks, with about every 13 stalks producing a bushel of corn. The seventh row has 88 corn stalks, with about every 11 stalks producing a bushel of corn. How many bushels of corn will Bob harvest in total?

As shown in the figure, color the five parts \( A, B, C, D, E \) with four different colors, such that adjacent parts cannot be colored the same color, while non-adjacent parts can be colored the same color. How many different ways can this figure be colored?

The volume of the parallelepiped determined by vectors $\mathbf{a}$, $\mathbf{b}$, and $\mathbf{c}$ is 6. Find the volume of the parallelepiped determined by $\mathbf{a} + 2\mathbf{b},$ $\mathbf{b} + \mathbf{c},$ and $2\mathbf{c} - 5\mathbf{a}.$

Let \( P \) be a polynomial with degree \( n \) such that \( \int_0^1 x^k P(x) \, dx = 0 \) for \( k = 1, 2, 3, \ldots, n \). Calculate the value of \( \frac{\int_0^1 P(x)^2 \, dx}{\left( \int_0^1 P(x) \, dx \right)^2} \) for \( n = 5 \).

Consider a circle divided into \( 2 \times 1399 \) equal sections and filled with the numbers \( 0, 1, 2, \dots, 1398 \) such that each number appears exactly twice. Let \( f(n) \) be the number of distinct arrangements of the numbers in the circle that satisfy the condition that for any \( a \), there are exactly \( a \) sections between the two sections that have the number \( a \) in them. Calculate \( f(1399) \).
What is the discriminant of the quadratic equation \(5x^2 - 11x + 2\)?

Let  $S$  be a square formed by the four vertices  $(1,1),(1.-1),(-1,1)$  and  $(-1,-1)$ . Let the region  $R$  be the set of points inside  $S$  which are closer to the center than any of the four sides. Find the area of the region  $R$ .

Let \(ABC\) be a triangle inscribed in a circle \((O)\) with incircle \((I)\) tangent to \(BC\), \(CA\), and \(AB\) at \(D\), \(E\), and \(F\) respectively. Let \(B_1 = BI \cap (O) \neq B\) and \(C_1 = CI \cap (O) \neq C\). Let \(EF \cap (O) = X_1, X_2\). Calculate the ratio of the length of the segment joining the circumcenter of \(\triangle DX_1X_2\) to the midpoint of \(C_1B_1\) to the radius of the circumcircle \((O)\).
There are some students in a class. Two-sevenths of them were absent last Monday, and 20 students were present. How many students are there in the class?

What is the smallest positive integer which, when divided by 4 gives a remainder of 3, when divided by 5 gives a remainder of 4, when divided by 6 gives a remainder of 5, and when divided by 7 gives a remainder of 6?
By choosing from the 10 women at the party, how many ways are there to assign the 5 men a dancing partner each such that exactly two men are dancing with their wives?

Adjacent sides of Figure 1 are perpendicular. Four sides of Figure 1 are removed to form Figure 2. In Figure 1, the perimeter on the left is 10 units and the right is 7 units. The top horizontal side before removal is 3 units, and the two smaller sections on the bottom are 2 and 1 units, respectively. What is the total length, in units, of the segments in Figure 2?

In the list 3, 3, 4, 4, 5, 5, 5, 5, 7, 11, 21, we want to determine the fraction of the data elements that are less than the mode. Also, we need to find the median of the data points only within the first quartile of the given list.

1. Calculate the mode of the given list of data elements.
2. Determine the fraction of data elements that are less than the mode.
3. Find the first quartile of the given data (Q1).
4. Calculate the median of the data elements within the first quartile.
the annual birth and death rate in a country per 1000 are 39.4 and 19.4 respectively . the number of years k in which the population would be doubled assuming there is no emigration or immigration is

There are 92 students altogether. Some of them ride the school bus home together, 5/8 of the remaining ride their own bike home, and the rest whose houses are near the school walk home. There are 27 students walking home. How many students ride the school bus home?

The numbers $p,$ $q,$ $r,$ $s$ are equal to 1, 5, 3, 6, in some order. Find the largest possible value of
\[pq + qr + rs + sp.\]

In an international chess competition, five classes (A, B, C, D, and E) each sent two participants. The rules state that participants do not compete with each other for more than one game and participants from the same class cannot compete with each other. After several rounds, all participants completed a different number of games except for the two participants from class A. How many games did the two participants from class A each complete?
If each bag has 41 cookies and you had 53 bags of cookies, how many cookies would you have?
For $k \geq 2$, let $S_k$ be the set of all limit points of the sequence $\{\sin^k(n)\}$. Calculate the length of the interval that contains $S_k$.

Let \(ABCD\) be a bicentric quadrilateral with circumcircle \((O, R)\) and incenter \(I\). If \(P\) is the intersection point of diagonals \(AC\) and \(BD\), and the distance \(IO = d\), calculate the value of \(OP\) given that \(R = 5\) and \(d = 3\).
Find the number of possible real solutions to the equation \((9+\sin x)^{f(x)}+(10+\sin x)^{f(x)}=(11+\sin x)^{f(x)}\) where \(f(x)=\frac{x}{1-x}\).
What is the sum of the two solutions to the equation $2x^2 - 8x - 10 = 0$?

In how many distinct ways can I arrange my six keys on a keychain, if I want to put my house key next to either my car key or my office key, but not both? Two arrangements are not considered different if the keys are in the same order (or can be made to be in the same order without taking the keys off the chain--that is, by reflection or rotation).
Let \(a, b, c > 0\). Find the maximum value of the expression \[\frac{1}{a(a+1)+bc}+\frac{1}{b(b+1)+ca}+\frac{1}{c(c+1)+ab}\] given that \(a + b + c = 3\).

The movie theater sells matinee tickets for $5, evening tickets for $12, and 3D tickets for $20. They sell 200 matinee tickets, a certain number of evening tickets, and 100 3D tickets. They make a total of $6600. How many evening tickets do they sell?

Let \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\) be non-negative numbers such that \(a^2 + b^2 + c^2 + abc = 4\). Calculate the maximum possible value of the expression \(6(a + b + c) - (abc + \sqrt{a^2 b^2 c^2 + 288})\).
Everyday Jonathan spends some hours on his phone. Half of this time is spent on social media. He spends 28 hours on social media in a week. How many hours does he spend on his phone daily?

For the graph of a quadratic \( y = ax^2 + bx + c \), the vertex of the parabola is \( (5,10) \) and one of the \( x \)-intercepts is \( (1,0) \). What is the \( x \)-coordinate of the other \( x \)-intercept?

Let \(a, b, c, d\) be positive real numbers such that \(a^2 + b^2 + c^2 + d^2 = a + b + c + d\). Find the minimum value of \(k\) such that the inequality \(a^3 + b^3 + c^3 + d^3 + k(a + b + c + d) \leq 4(1 + k)\) holds.
Diana needs to bike 10 miles to get home.  She can bike 3 mph for two hours before she gets tired, and she can bike 1 mph until she gets home.  How long will it take Diana to get home?
A train has a certain speed. It covers a distance of 20 km in 20 minutes. What is the speed of the train in kmph?

Madison makes some paper boats and sets them afloat. 20% are eaten by fish and Madison shoots two of the others with flaming arrows. There are 22 boats left. How many paper boats did Madison make initially?
Let \( P(x) \) be the polynomial of minimum degree such that \( P(k) = \frac{1}{k(k+1)} \) for \( k = 1, 2, \ldots, 10 \). What is \( P(11) \)?

Charles bought some papers to draw. Today Charles drew 6 pictures. Yesterday he drew 6 pictures before going to work and 6 pictures when he came back. He has 2 papers left. How many papers did Charles buy initially?

The number  $\frac{1}{2}$  is written on a blackboard. Let the walking speed of the hiker on the first day be x miles per hour, and let the number of hours she walked on the first day be y hours. Given that she walked 18 miles on the first day, we have:

x*y = 18 (1)

On the second day, the hiker walked for one less hour (y - 1) and one mile per hour faster (x + 1) than on the first day. Let the total distance she walked on the second day be D2.

D2 = (y - 1) * (x + 1) (2)

On the third day, the walking speed of the hiker was 5 miles per hour and she walked for 3 hours. Let the total distance she walked on the third day be D3. Then,

D3 = 5 * 3 (3)

Now, let's add an additional constraint to make the problem more challenging. Let's say the hiker wants to achieve an overall average speed of Z miles per hour throughout the 3 days.

The overall distance (D_total) the hiker walked is the sum of the distances she walked each day:

D_total = 18 + D2 + D3

The overall time (T_total) the hiker spent walking is the sum of the hours she walked each day:

T_total = y + (y - 1) + 3

Now, we have the equation for the overall average speed (Z) the hiker wants to achieve:

Z = D_total / T_total

Now, we have introduced variables for walking speed (x), hours walked each day (y), and an additional constraint (Z). Calculate the total distance the hiker walked based on these variables and constraints.

If \( \| f \|_{1} = 1 \), find the smallest possible value of \( C \) such that \( m(A) \leq \frac{C}{A} \) for all \( A > 0 \).

Let \(ABCD\) be a complete quadrangle with \(AB \times CD = E\) and \(AD \times BC = F\). Consider three point-pairs \(P, X\); \(Q, Y\); and \(R, Z\) on \(AC\), \(DB\), and \(EF\) respectively such that \((AC, PX) = (DB, QY) = (EF, RZ)\). If \(P, Q, R\) are collinear, find the value of \(\frac{PX}{AC} + \frac{QY}{DB} + \frac{RZ}{EF}\).
If \(a, b, x\), and \(y\) are real numbers such that \(a x + b y = 3\), \(a x^{2} + b y^{2} = 7\), \(a x^{3} + b y^{3} = 16\), and \(a x^{4} + b y^{4} = 42\), find \(a x^{5} + b y^{5}\).
Let \(\mathbf{X} = \begin{pmatrix} p & q & r \\ s & t & u \\ v & w & x \end{pmatrix}\), where \(\mathbf{X}^T = \mathbf{X}^{-1}\). Find \(p^2 + q^2 + r^2 + s^2 + t^2 + u^2 + v^2 + w^2 + x^2.\)

Let \( n \geq 1 \) and \( A \in M_n(\mathbb{C}) \) be an invertible matrix that is not cyclic. If \( A \) admits an infinity of square roots, find the minimum number of distinct square roots \( B \) such that \( B^2 = A \) and \( B \neq -B \).

Let \( \gamma_1 \) and \( \gamma_2 \) be two circles that intersect at points \( A \) and \( B \). A moving line \( (\triangle) \) passes through \( A \) and intersects \( \gamma_1 \) at \( P_1 \) and \( \gamma_2 \) at \( P_2 \). Let \( M \) be the midpoint of segment \( [P_1P_2] \) and \( O \) be the intersection of the perpendicular bisector of \( [P_1P_2] \) and the line \( AB \). If the radius of \( \gamma_1 \) is 10 and the radius of \( \gamma_2 \) is 15, find the length of \( OB \).

A certain debt will be paid in some installments from January 1 to December 31 of a certain year. Each of the first 20 payments is to be $410; each of the remaining payments is to be $65 more than each of the first 20 payments. The average (arithmetic mean) payment that will be made on the debt for the year is $442.5. How many installments are there in total?
If the length of the longest chord of a certain circle is 10, what is the radius of that certain circle?
a is half good a work man as b and together they finish a job in 26 days . in how many days working alone b finish the job ?

The cost of the paint is Rs. 40.00 per kg. If 1 kg of paint covers 20 sq. ft, how much will it cost to paint the outside of a cube having a certain length for each side, given that the total cost is Rs. 1200?

Given a $101$-digit number $a$ and an arbitrary positive integer $b$, let $N$ be the largest $102$-digit positive integer $c$ such that any number of the form $\overline{caaa \dots ab}$ is composite. Find the sum of the digits of $N$.
A lady builds a box with 12 cm length, 16 cm width, and a certain height using 3 cubic cm cubes. The minimum number of cubes required to build the box is 384. What is the height of the box?

Dream's car consumes 4 gallons of gas per mile. If she drives a certain distance today and 200 more miles tomorrow than today, the car will consume 4000 gallons of gas. How many miles did she drive today?
What least number should be subtracted from 3,381 so that the remainder when divided by 9, 11, and 17 will leave in each case the same remainder 8?

Consider the statement: "If a triangle has sides of lengths $a$, $b$, and $c$, and $a^2 + b^2 = c^2$, then the triangle is a right triangle." 

Let $P$ be the number of distinct integer triples $(a, b, c)$ such that $1 \leq a, b, c \leq 100$ and $a^2 + b^2 = c^2$. 

Find $P$.

Ali has a store that sells fruits and vegetables. He puts 23 kg of kidney apples, some kg of golden apples, and 14 kg of Canada apples on the shelves. By noon, 36 kg of apples were sold. He has 38 kg of apples left. How many kg of golden apples did he put on the shelves?

John skateboarded for 16 miles, then walked another 8 miles, and finally biked for 6 miles to the park. Before leaving the park, he jogged for 3 miles around the park's perimeter. John then took a different route back home, which involved biking for 5 miles, swimming across a 1-mile wide river, and skateboarding the last 9 miles. How many miles has John skateboarded in total for his entire journey?
Evaluate $\lfloor \sqrt{50} \rfloor ^2 + 2$.

A cube has edge length \( 4 \text{ m} \). One end of a rope of length \( 5 \text{ m} \) is anchored to the centre of the top face of the cube. The area of the surface of the cube that can be reached by the other end of the rope is \( A \text{ m}^2 \). What is the integer formed by the rightmost two digits of the integer closest to \( 100A \)?
Fangfang has a total of 30 coins, consisting of 1-jiao and 5-jiao coins, amounting to 8 yuan and 6 jiao. How many coins of each type does she have?

We drew the incircle and the excircles of a triangle, as well as the six lines that touch two of these circles each, but are distinct from the sides of the triangle. How many ways can one choose from these six lines:

a) the side lines of a trapezoid,

b) the side lines of a parallelogram, assuming that none of the sides of the original triangle are equal in length?

There are 87 oranges and some bananas in Philip's collection. The bananas are organized into 2 groups and oranges are organized into 93 groups. Each group of bananas has 145 bananas. How many bananas are in Philip's collection?

Two teams of 3 swimmers each are in a pool with seven lanes. No two swimmers from the same team are allowed to be in adjacent lanes. Compute the number of possible arrangements if the swimmers themselves are distinguishable.
There are 9 pencils and 4 rulers in the drawer. Sally took 4 pencils out of the drawer. How many pencils are there now?

Let \( P(x) = a_{1998}x^{1998} + a_{1997}x^{1997} + \cdots + a_1x + a_0 \) be a polynomial with real coefficients such that \( P(0) \ne P(-1) \). Let \( a \) and \( b \) be real numbers, and define \( Q(x) = b_{1998}x^{1998} + b_{1997}x^{1997} + \cdots + b_1x + b_0 \) where \( b_k = aa_k + b \) for all \( k = 0, 1, 2, \ldots, 1998 \). Given that \( Q(0) = Q(-1) \ne 0 \), find the value of \( \frac{a_{1998}}{a_{1997}} \) if \( a = 2 \) and \( b = -1 \).

If a, b, and c together can finish a piece of work in 4 days, a alone in 12 days, and b in some days, then c alone can do it in 8.999999999999998 days. How many days does b alone take to finish the work?

Given 6 points $A_1, \ldots, A_6$ on a circle $(O)$ and a point $M$ on the plane. Let $C_1, \ldots, C_6$ be the circumcenters of triangles $MA_1A_2, \ldots, MA_6A_1$. Let $B_1$ be a point on $(C_1)$, $B_1A_2$ cuts $(C_2)$ again at $B_2$, ..., $B_5A_6$ cuts $(C_6)$ again at $B_6$. If $B_6A_1$ cuts $(C_1)$ again at $B_1$ and the hexagons $B_1B_2\ldots B_6$ and $C_1C_2\ldots C_6$ are similar, find the ratio of the areas of hexagons $B_1B_2\ldots B_6$ and $C_1C_2\ldots C_6$.

Two rectangles, one measuring $2 \times 4$ and another measuring $3 \times 5$, along with a circle of diameter 3, are to be contained within a square. The sides of the square are parallel to the sides of the rectangles and the circle must not overlap any rectangle at any point internally. What is the smallest possible area of the square?

The measures of angles \( A \) and \( B \) are both positive, integer numbers of degrees. The measure of angle \( A \) is a multiple of the measure of angle \( B \), and angles \( A \) and \( B \) are supplementary angles. How many measures are possible for angle \( A \)?
Let $f(x)=\left\{\begin{array}{l}\sqrt{x-1}(x\geq1)\\ 1,(x<1)\end{array}\right.$, then $f\left(f\left(f\left(2\right)\right)\right)=\_\_\_\_\_\_.$

Given a sequence \( a_i \geq 0 \) for \( i=1, \ldots, 100 \) such that \( a_1 \geq a_2 \geq a_3 \geq \ldots \geq a_{100} \), and the conditions:
\[ a_1 + a_2 \leq 100 \]
\[ a_3 + a_4 + \ldots + a_{100} \leq 100 \]
Find the maximum value of \( S = \sum_{i=1}^{100} a_i^2 \).
15 consecutive natural numbers lie between a certain natural number and 81. What is this natural number when it is less than 81?

All four-digit numbers from 1000 to 9999 are written consecutively without spaces. Kostya underlined $k$ digits in a row in this sequence, and Andrey underlined another $k$ digits in a row in this sequence. It turned out that the $k$-digit numbers underlined by the boys were equal. What is the largest possible $k$ for which this could happen?

Find the volume of the region in space defined by
\[ |x + y + 2z| + |x + y - 2z| \le 12 \]
and \(x, y, z \ge 0\).
How many terms of the arithmetic sequence 88, 85, 82, $\dots$ appear before the number $-17$ appears?

In a class of 25 students, students were asked if they like French fries, burgers, or neither. 15 students said they like French fries and 10 said they like burgers, with these statistics including the responses of 6 students who said they like both French fries and burgers. How many students do not like either food?

Consider an abelian subgroup \( W \) of \( P \) generated by all elements \( f(x, y) \). If \( (W, f) \) is a tensor product, calculate the number of generators needed to express \( W \) as a direct sum of cyclic groups when \( P \) is a finite abelian group of order \( 2^{10} \cdot 3^5 \cdot 5^3 \).

Andy works in the pro shop at a tennis resort, where he earns $9 an hour. In addition to this, he gets paid $15 for each racquet he restrings, $10 for changing out the grommets on a racquet, and $1 for painting a stencil on the racquet strings. He earns $202 (before taxes) during an 8-hour shift if he strings a certain number of racquets, changes 2 sets of grommets, and paints 5 stencils. How many racquets did he restring during that shift?
At Joe's Fruit Stand, 5 bananas cost as much as 3 apples, and 8 apples cost as much as 5 oranges. How many oranges cost as much as 25 bananas?
For each positive integer \( n \), let \( S(n) \) be the smallest positive value of \( x+y+z \) such that \( x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = 59^n \) where \( x, y, z \) are integers. Find \( S(3) \).

Let \( L: V \to V \) be a linear transformation of rank 1. Define \( c \) as the scalar such that \( L^2 = cL \). If \( L(v) = w \) for some nonzero vectors \( v, w \in V \), find the value of \( c \) in terms of \( v \) and \( w \).
What is the greatest common divisor of 45, 75, and 105?
Dan's car gets a certain mileage per gallon. If gas costs $4/gallon, then Dan's car can go 304 miles on $38 of gas. How many miles per gallon does Dan's car get?

Karlsson can eat no more than 5 kg of jam in one meal. If he opens a new jar of jam, he must eat it completely during that meal (Karlsson will not open a new jar if he would have to eat more than 5 kg of jam in total, including what he has just eaten).

Malysh has several jars of raspberry jam weighing a total of 50 kg, with each jar weighing no more than 1 kg. What is the minimum number of meals Karlsson will need to eat all the jam?

A girl has the following seven coins in her pocket: $2$ pennies, $2$ nickels, $1$ dime, $1$ quarter, and $1$ half-dollar. She takes out two coins, records the sum of their values, and then puts them back with the other coins. She continues to take out two coins, record the sum of their values, and put them back. How many different sums can she record at most?
Sue borrowed 15 books and 6 movies. She returned 8 books. She then returned a third of the movies to the library and checked out 9 more books. How many movies and books does Sue now have?

The function $g(x)$ satisfies
\[g(x + y) = g(x) g(y)\] for all real numbers $x$ and $y.$ If $g(3) = 4,$ find $g(9).$
A restaurant made 9 hamburgers to serve during lunch. They quickly sold those and had to make 3 more. How many hamburgers did they make for lunch in total?
A ball is thrown such that its height above ground, in feet, after $t$ seconds is given by the equation $h(t) = -20t^2 + 80t + 20$. Determine the maximum height achieved by the ball.

In a specific sequence, the first term is $a_1 = 1007$ and the second term is $a_2 = 1008$. The values of subsequent terms are set such that
\[ a_n + a_{n+1} + a_{n+2} = 2n \]
for all $n \geq 1$. Determine the value of $a_{1000}$.

A student mistakenly added seven to both the numerator and the denominator of a fraction, changing the fraction's value to $\frac{1}{3}$. If the original numerator was 3, what was the original denominator?

Consider a triangle \(ABC\) with its circumcircle \((O)\). The incircle of triangle \(ABC\) touches its sides at points \(M, N, P\). Let \(H\) be the orthocenter and \(G\) be the centroid of triangle \(MNP\). If the distance from \(O\) to line \(HG\) is \(d\), find the value of \(d\) when the circumradius of triangle \(ABC\) is \(R\) and the inradius is \(r\).
Two trains are moving in the same direction at 220 kmph and 42 kmph. The faster train crosses a man in the slower train in 25 seconds. Find the length of the faster train.
In a convex quadrilateral \(ABCD\), let \(AB = a\), \(BC = b\), \(CD = c\), and \(DA = d\). Calculate the minimum value of the expression \(\frac{(ab+cd)^2 + (bc+da)^2}{(ac+bd)^2}\).

In a company of 148 employees, 92 are females. A total of 78 employees have advanced degrees and the rest have a college degree only. If some employees are males with college degree only, then 53 employees are females with advanced degrees. How many males have only a college degree?

A sequence is defined as follows  $a_1=a_2=a_3=1$ , and, for all positive integers  $n$ ,  $a_{n+3}=a_{n+2}+a_{n+1}+a_n$ . Given that  $a_{28}=6090307$ ,  $a_{29}=11201821$ , and  $a_{30}=20603361$ , find the remainder when  $\displaystyle \sum^{28}_{k=1} a_k$  is divided by 1000.

Assume that $\sum\limits_{n=1}^{\infty} a_n$ diverges ($a_n>0$). Define $S_n=a_1+a_2+...+a_n$. Calculate the value of $\sum\limits_{n=1}^{1000}\dfrac{a_n}{S_n}$ given that $a_n = \frac{1}{n}$ for all $n$.

A certain store sells two pieces of clothing at a price of $180$ yuan each at a certain time. One piece makes a profit of $20\%$, while the other piece incurs a loss of $10\%$. The total profit made by the store from selling these two pieces of clothing is ______ yuan.

Nathan wants to line the inside of a box with velvet. The box has two long sides that measure 8 inches by 6 inches, two short sides that measure 5 inches by six inches and a top and a bottom that each measure some square inches. Nathan needs 236 square inches of velvet. What is the area of the top and bottom of the box?
There were 9 people in line for bumper cars. If 6 people got tired of waiting and left, but 3 more people got in line, how many people were in line at some point?
The circumference of a Polaroid photo is 40 centimeters (cm). Find the length of the length when the width is 8 centimeters (cm).
Twenty-four is 48% of what number?
A very large number \( y \) is equal to \( 2^33^44^55^66^77^88^9 \). What is the smallest positive integer that, when multiplied with \( y \), produces a product that is a perfect square?
Adah practiced the cello for a total of 7.5 hours last week. He practiced for 86 minutes on each of 2 days. How many minutes in total did he practice on the other days?
The sum of the first $n$ terms of an arithmetic sequence is 2000. The common difference is 2, and the first term is an integer with $n > 1$. Find the sum of all possible values of $n$.

The cardinality of a finite set \\(P\\) is denoted as \\(\text{card}(P)\\). It is known that \\(\text{card}(M) = 10\\), \\(A \subseteq M\\), \\(B \subseteq M\\), \\(A \cap B = \varnothing\\), and \\(\text{card}(A) = 2\\), \\(\text{card}(B) = 3\\).

\\((1)\\) If set \\(X\\) satisfies \\(A \subseteq X \subseteq M\\), find the number of such sets \\(X\\).

\\((2)\\) If set \\(Y\\) satisfies \\(Y \subseteq M\\), \\(A \not\subset Y\\), \\(B \not\subset Y\\), find the number of such sets \\(Y\\).
the width of a rectangular hall is ½ of its length . if the area of the hall is 800 sq . m , what is the difference between its length and breadth ?
Determine the number of integer solutions for the equation \( 2^{2x} - 5^{2y} = 75 \) where \( x \) and \( y \) are integers.

There exists a point \( M \) inside an equilateral triangle \( ABC \) such that the perpendiculars \( MX \), \( MY \), and \( MZ \) are drawn to the sides \( AB \), \( BC \), and \( AC \) respectively. The ratios of the lengths \( MX : MY : MZ \) is \( 1 : 2 : 3 \). Let \( \frac{[MYBX]}{[\triangle ABC]} = \frac{m}{n} \) where \( m \) and \( n \) are relatively prime positive integers. Find \( m + n \).

A big square is dissected by $10$ horizontal and $10$ vertical lines into $100$ rectangular pieces. If exactly $9$ of these pieces are squares, find the minimum number of congruent square pieces among these $9$ squares.

For a positive integer $n$, let $S(n)$ denote the value of $\sum_{r=2}^{n} \left \lfloor n^{\frac{1}{r}} \right \rfloor - \sum_{r=2}^{n} \left \lfloor \log_{r}(n) \right \rfloor$. Calculate $S(2023)$.

Let \( S \) be the set of integers \( k \) consisting of nonzero digits, such that \( 300 < k < 400 \) and \( k - 300 \) is not divisible by \( 11 \). For each \( k \) in \( S \), let \( A(k) \) denote the set of integers in \( S \) not equal to \( k \) that can be formed by permuting the digits of \( k \). Find the number of integers \( k \) in \( S \) such that \( k \) is relatively prime to all elements of \( A(k) \).
What is the minimum number of circles with a unit radius required to completely cover a triangle with sides 2, 3, and 4?

In the 2013 Zhejiang College Entrance Examination, arrange the six letters A, B, C, D, E, F in a row, with both A and B on the same side of C. How many different arrangements are there? (Answer with a number.)

Jason had some Pokemon cards. He gave a certain number of Pokemon cards to his friends and now has 4 Pokemon cards left. He started with 13 Pokemon cards. How many Pokemon cards did he give to his friends?

Let \( r(x) \) have domain \( \{-2, -1, 0, 1\} \) and range \( \{-1, 0, 3, 5\} \). Let \( s(x) \) have domain \( \{0, 1, 2, 3\} \) and be defined by \( s(x) = x^2 + 2x + 1 \). What is the sum of all possible values of \( s(r(x)) \)?
Let \( z_1 \) and \( z_2 \) be two complex numbers that satisfy \( |iz + \sqrt{2} - i| = 1 \) and \( |z_1 - z_2| = 2 \). Find the maximum value of \( P = |z_1| + |z_2| \).

Evaluate the expression $\frac{1}{2\cos 1}\int_1^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\frac{\sin x}{x}\, \text{d}x$ and compare it to $\frac{\ln \pi - \ln 2}{\pi - 2}$. If the inequality holds, compute the value of $\left\lfloor 100 \left( \frac{\ln \pi - \ln 2}{\pi - 2} - \frac{1}{2\cos 1}\int_1^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\frac{\sin x}{x}\, \text{d}x \right) \right\rfloor$.

a is 1.5 times as fast as b. a alone can do the work in 30 days. Worker c is 2 times as fast as b, and worker d is 0.5 times as fast as a. If a and b work on alternating days, while c and d work together on the remaining days, in how many days will the work be completed?
Let \(A = (2,0), B = (5,2),\) and \(C = (p, q)\) be three points on the parabola \(y = x^2 - 4x + 3\) where \(2 \le p \le 5.\) Find the largest possible area of triangle \(ABC.\)

Given that \( \mathrm{a}, \mathrm{b}, \mathrm{c} \) are three natural numbers, and the least common multiple (LCM) of \( \mathrm{a} \) and \( \mathrm{b} \) is 60, and the LCM of \( \mathrm{a} \) and \( \mathrm{c} \) is 270, find the LCM of \( \mathrm{b} \) and \( \mathrm{c} \).

Given a convex quadrilateral $ABCD$ and a point $N$ in its interior such that $|AN| = |DN| = 8$, $|BN| = |CN| = 6$, and $|\angle DNB| = |\angle ANC| = 120^\circ$. Find the area of the quadrilateral $ABCD$ for $|\angle ANB| = 30^\circ$.
Given $\sum_{i=1}^{n} a_i = 6$, find the maximum value of the expression $2a_1 + \sum_{k=2}^{n} \prod_{i=1}^{k} a_i$.

Let \( S = \{a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h\} \). Find the maximum \( n \) such that \( A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_n \) are distinct 4-element subsets of \( S \), and \( |A_i \cap A_j| = 2 \) for all distinct \( i, j \).
Given that $x=1$ is a solution to the equation $2ax-2=a+3$, then $a=$    .

Values for $A,B,C,$ and $D$ are to be selected from ${1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}$ without replacement (i.e. no two letters have the same value). How many ways are there to make such choices so that the two curves $y=Ax^2+B$ and $y=Cx^2+D$ intersect? (The order in which the curves are listed does not matter.)
Plot the set of points on the plane \((x, y)\) that satisfy the equation \( |3x| + |4y| + |48 - 3x - 4y| = 48 \), and find the area of the resulting figure.
at an election 2 candidates are participated a candidate got 30 % of votes and defeated by 5000 votes . 100 votes are invalid . find the total polled votes ?
Find the last two digits of the following sum: $$3! + 7! + 11! + 15! + \cdots + 99!$$
A man has Rs. 10350 in the form of Rs. 50 notes and Rs. 500 notes. He has 37 notes of Rs. 50 denomination. What is the total number of notes he has?

Let \((a_n)\) be a sequence of positive integers such that \(a_0 = 2\), \(a_1 = 3\), and for all \(n \geq 2\), \(n(a_{n-1} - 1) + a_n = \frac{a_{n+1}}{n+1} + 1\). Find all prime numbers \(p, q, r\) such that \(a_p \cdot a_q \cdot a_r\) is a power of a prime number.
Find the area enclosed by the curve $y=3-3x^{2}$ and the $x$-axis.
Consider a scouter sequence $\{a_n\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$. Define $g(n)$ as the number of divisor-unfriendly indices $i$ in the range $1 \le i \le n$. Find the minimum possible value of $g(100)$.

For every positive \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\) such that \(a^2 + b^2 + c^2 = 1\), find the minimum value of the expression:
\[
\sum \frac{a}{a^3 + bc}
\]
If $(x^2 - 4) + (x^2 + 3x + 2)i$ is a pure imaginary number, find the value of the real number $x$.

Suppose that \( p \) and \( q \) are rational roots of the equation \( x^2 - x + c = 0 \), where \( c \in \mathbb{R} \). If \( r \) and \( s \) are the roots of the equation \( x^2 + px - q = 0 \), calculate the value of \( r^2 + s^2 \).
The sequence ${a_n}$ satisfies $a_1=1$, $a_{2n+1}+a_{2n}=n+1$. The sum of the first 21 terms of the sequence ${a_n}$ is ___.

Lyle wants to buy himself and his friends a sandwich and a pack of juice. A sandwich costs $0.30 while a pack of juice costs $0.2. If Lyle has $2.50, how many of his friends can have a sandwich and a pack of juice?
Determine how many values of $c$ in the interval $[0, 2000]$ does the equation \[9 \lfloor x \rfloor + 3 \lceil x \rceil = c\] have a solution for $x$?
A company invited 18 people to a luncheon, but some of them didn't show up. If the tables they had held 3 people each, and they needed 2 tables, how many people didn't show up?

Suppose the numbers \[4 - \sqrt{5}, \; -4 - \sqrt{5}, \; 2 + 2\sqrt{3}, \; 2 - 2\sqrt{3}\] are roots of the same nonzero polynomial with rational coefficients. Determine the smallest possible degree of the polynomial.
Define the sequence \(a_1 = 1\), \(a_2, a_3, \ldots \) by \(a_{n+1} = a_1^2 + a_2^2 + a_3^2 + \ldots + a_n^2 + n\). Show that 1 is the only square in the sequence.
a jar contains 18 balls . 3 blue balls are removed from the jar and not replaced . now the probability of getting a blue ball is 1 / 5 then how many blue balls jar contains initially ?

Consider the set of all points $(x,y)$ in the coordinate plane for which one of the coordinates is exactly twice the other or equal to the other. If we were to plot all such points, into how many regions would the resulting graph split up the plane?

in a certain supermarket , a triangular display of cans is arranged in 9 rows , numbered 1 through 9 from top to bottom . each successively numbered row contains 3 more cans than the row immediately above it . if there are fewer than 120 cans in the entire display , how many cans are in the seventh row ?
Eric has 3 boxes of pencils. Each box holds a certain number of pencils. Eric has 27 pencils in total. How many pencils does each box hold?

There are 25 students in the orchestra, 40 in the band, 30 in the choir, and 15 in the jazz ensemble. Some students participate in more than one group. 5 students are in both the orchestra and the band, 6 students are in both the orchestra and the choir, 4 students are in both the band and the choir, and 3 students are in both the band and the jazz ensemble. Additionally, 2 students are in both the orchestra and the jazz ensemble, and 4 students are in both the choir and the jazz ensemble. There are also 3 students who participate in the orchestra, the band, and the choir, and 1 student who participates in all four groups.

Considering the overlapping membership between the groups, how many unique students are there in the orchestra, the band, the choir, and the jazz ensemble?

Twelve machines, each working at the same constant rate, together can complete a certain job in a certain number of days. If six additional machines are added, they can complete the job in 8 days. How many days does it take for the initial twelve machines to complete the job?

In triangle \( \triangle ABC \), let \( AH \perp BC \) with \( H \in BC \), \( BN \perp AC \) with \( N \in AC \), and \( CM \perp AB \) with \( M \in AB \). Points \( D \) and \( F \) are on \( BN \) and \( CM \) respectively such that \( \angle ADC = \angle AFB = 90^\circ \). Let \( K = BN \cap CM \), \( I = BF \cap CD \), and \( P = BC \cap KI \). Calculate the value of \( \frac{\angle DHF}{\angle DPF} \).

There are 10 players in a chess group, and each player plays each of the others a certain number of times. Given that each game is played by two players, there will be a total of 45 games played. How many times does each player play the others?
In triangle \(ABC\), \(AB = 28\), \(BC = 21\), and \(CA = 14\). Points \(D\) and \(E\) are on \(AB\) such that \(AD = 7\) and \(\angle ACD = \angle BCE\). Find the length of \(BE\).
Given $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$, and $a \neq -1$, the minimum value of $\left| a+b \right|+\left| \frac{1}{a+1}-b \right|$ is __________.

In the first week of August, Jordan gave Danielle four gifts on four separate days: on the first day, he gave her 3 dozen roses; on the second day, 5 boxes of chocolates; on the third day, 10 assorted cupcakes; and on the fourth day, 2 dozens of sunflowers.

For the following three days, Danielle made several trades with her friend Alice:

- On the fifth day, Danielle traded one box of chocolates for another dozen roses and half a dozen sunflowers.
- On the sixth day, she traded three boxes of chocolates for 20 cupcakes and another dozen roses.
- On the seventh day, Danielle traded the remaining box of chocolates for 15 daffodils.
  
Over this week, some of the flowers started to wilt:

- On the fifth day, 10% of Danielle's roses wilted, and she threw them away.
- On the sixth day, 20% of the remaining roses and 30% of the sunflowers wilted, and she threw them away.
- On the seventh day, 25% of the remaining roses, 15% of the remaining sunflowers, and 20% of daffodils wilted, and Danielle threw them away.

Calculate the number of unwilted roses, sunflowers, and daffodils Danielle had at the end of the seventh day.

A swimmer can swim a certain distance against the current of a river which flows at 1.7 km/hr, given that he can swim in still water at 3 km/h. It takes him 2.3076923076923075 hours to swim the distance. What is the distance he swam against the current?

Set $\Phi$ consists of points on the plane such that the distance between any two points is at least $\sqrt{2}$. All points in $\Phi$ can be covered by an equilateral triangle with side length 3. Find the maximum possible number of points in $\Phi$.

A painter needed to paint some rooms in a building. Each room takes 8 hours to paint. He already painted 8 rooms and will take 16 hours to paint the rest. How many rooms does he need to paint in total?
A square of size \( n \times n \) was cut into squares of sizes \( 40 \times 40 \) and \( 49 \times 49 \) such that squares of both types appeared. What is the minimal possible value of \( n \)?
Celine collected twice as many erasers as Gabriel did. Julian collected twice as many erasers as Celine did. If they collected 35 erasers in total, how many erasers did Celine collect?

(1) If a teacher and 6 students are to line up in a row, with the condition that the teacher cannot stand at either end, how many different arrangements are possible?  
(2) From 6 boys and 5 girls, 4 people are to be selected to participate in a competition, with the condition that there must be at least one boy and one girl among them. How many different selections are possible?  
(3) Originally, there are 3 programs on a schedule. If the relative order of these 3 programs remains unchanged, and 2 new programs are added, how many different arrangements are possible?

A scanning code consists of a $5 \times 5$ grid of squares, with at least one square of each color (black or white). A code is symmetric if it looks the same after a rotation of $180^\circ$ and after reflection across the horizontal and vertical lines through the center. How many such symmetric scanning codes are possible?
For positive integers \( x \), let \( g(x) \) be the number of blocks of consecutive \( 1 \)'s in the binary expansion of \( x \). Compute \( g(1) + g(2) + g(3) + \cdots + g(256) \).

p and q are the only two applicants qualified for a short-term research project that pays 480 dollars in total. Candidate p has more experience and, if hired, would be paid 50 percent more per hour than candidate q would be paid. Candidate q, if hired, would require a certain number of hours more than candidate p to do the job. Candidate p's hourly wage is 8 dollars greater than candidate q's hourly wage. How many more hours would candidate q require to do the job compared to candidate p?

In a game, $C$ produces three random integers $1 \leq a, b, c \leq 100$. $A$ knows $a$ and $100$, and $B$ knows $b$ and $100$. $C$ tells $A$ the numbers $a+b$ and $b+c$, and tells $B$ the numbers $a+b$ and $a+c$. $C$ asks $A$ for the value of $b$. If $A$ does not know, $C$ asks $B$ for the value of $a$. If $B$ does not know, the process repeats with $A$ and $B$ hearing each other's responses (yes or no). Let $k$ be the number of rounds required for one of them to correctly determine the value of the unknown variable. Find the maximum possible value of $k$.
Luna, Ginny, Hermione, and Cho are competing in a spell-casting contest. Assuming there are no ties, in how many different possible orders can they finish?
What is the digit sum of the number of ways to place 45 different types of chocolates in 3 identical bags such that each bag has at least one chocolate?

Vertices of a square \(ABCD\) with side length \(\frac{25}{4}\) lie on a sphere. Parallel lines passing through points \(A, B, C,\) and \(D\) intersect the sphere at points \(A_1, B_1, C_1,\) and \(D_1\), respectively. Given that \(AA_1 = 2\), \(BB_1 = 10\), and \(CC_1 = 6\), determine the length of the segment \(DD_1\).
When the square root of $x$ is raised to the fourth power, the answer is 256. What is the value of $x$?

Consider an infinite sequence $\{ a_n \}_{n \ge 0}$ of real numbers satisfying $a_n \ge n^2$. For each $i, j \ge 0$, there exist $k, l$ with $(i,j) \neq (k,l)$, $l - k = j - i$, and $a_l - a_k = a_j - a_i$. Find the smallest integer $N$ such that $a_n \ge (n + N)^2$ for some $n$.

The faces of eight unit cubes are colored black and white so that there are equally many black and white faces. Form a $2 \times 2 \times 2$ cube from these unit cubes such that there are equally many white and black faces on its surface. Let $N$ be the number of distinct ways to achieve this, considering rotations as identical. Calculate $N$.

For certain real values of $a, b, c,$ and $d,$ the equation $x^4 + ax^3 + bx^2 + cx + d = 0$ has four non-real roots. The product of two of these roots is $7 + 2i$ and the sum of the other two roots is $-1 + 3i,$ where $i^2 = -1.$ Find $b.$

Lark has forgotten her locker combination. It is a sequence of three numbers, each in the range from 1 to 30, except the third number, which is in the range from 1 to 40. She knows that the first number is odd, the second number is even, and the third number is a multiple of 5. How many combinations could possibly be Lark’s?
Given positive real numbers \(a_1, a_2, \cdots, a_n\) such that \(\Pi_{i=1}^{n} a_i = 1\), calculate the minimum value of the expression \(\sum_{i=1}^{n} \frac{1}{a_i + n - 1}\).

Let $a$, $b$, and $c$ be positive real numbers. Find the minimum value of
\[
\frac{a^2}{b^2} + \frac{b^2}{c^2} + \frac{c^2}{a^2}.
\]
If $\frac{5}{2} (x + y + z) = 15$, what is the average of $x$, $y$, and $z$?

A jewelry store is restocking its shelves. The necklace stand, which can hold 12 necklaces, currently holds 5 necklaces. The ring display can hold a certain number of rings and currently holds 18 rings. The bracelet display, which can hold 15 bracelets, currently holds 8 bracelets. The store’s supplier charges $4 per necklace, $10 per ring, and $5 per bracelet. The store needs to pay $183 to fill the displays. How many rings can the ring display hold?

Given an arithmetic progression of positive integers \(a_1 < a_2 < \ldots < a_n\) where \(a_1\) and the arithmetic ratio are coprime, let \(P = a_1 a_2 \ldots a_n\) and \(L = \text{lcm}(a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n)\). Find the smallest possible value of \(n\) such that \(P\) divides \((n-1)! \cdot L\).

Assume that the four numbers \[2 - \sqrt{3}, \; -2 - \sqrt{3}, \; \sqrt{5} - 2, \; 2 - \sqrt{5}\] are roots of the same nonzero polynomial with rational coefficients. What is the smallest possible degree of this polynomial?

Given \( n \) points with no three points collinear, each pair of points is connected by a line segment, and each line segment is colored with either red or blue. If for any coloring, there are certainly 12 monochromatic triangles, find the minimum value of \( n \).
Tiffany had 6 pages of math homework and some pages of reading homework. Each page had 3 problems on it. She had to complete 30 problems total. How many pages of reading homework did she have?

Nine digits: \(1, 2, 3, \ldots, 9\) are written in a certain order (forming a nine-digit number). Consider all consecutive triples of digits, and find the sum of the resulting seven three-digit numbers. What is the largest possible value of this sum?
Let \( n \) be a positive integer such that \( (2^n - 1)(3^n - 1) = k^2 \) for some integer \( k \). Find the sum of all possible values of \( n \) for which \( k \) is an integer.

Given that the function $f(x)$ satisfies $f(x+2)=f(x)$ for any real number $x∈R$, and $f(x)=2^{x+a}$ when $x∈[-1,1]$. If the point $P(2017,8)$ is on the graph of the function, find the value of the real number $a$.

Let $a,$ $b,$ and $c$ be positive real numbers and let $k$ be a positive constant. Find the minimum value of
\[
\frac{a + b + k}{c} + \frac{a + c + k}{b} + \frac{b + c + k}{a}.
\]
How many zeros are in the expansion of $999,\!999,\!999,\!98^2$?
An alien creature reported that it has stored $263_7$ units of energy. How many units is this in base 10?
What is the divisor if the dividend is 139, the quotient is 7, and the remainder is 6?
Find the remainder when the number of 6-digit "gross" numbers (numbers that contain the digits $1$, $4$, $4$ in that order, but not necessarily consecutively) is divided by $1000$.
Hyewon made pentagonal pillars with clay during art class and painted each side with a different color. How many colors did Hyewon paint on the pentagonal pillar?

Let \(ABC\) be a triangle with \(\angle BAC \ne 45^\circ\) and \(\angle ABC \ne 135^\circ\). Let \(P\) be the point on the line \(AB\) such that \(\angle CPB = 45^\circ\). Let \(O_1\) and \(O_2\) be the centers of the circumcircles of triangles \(ACP\) and \(BCP\) respectively. If the area of triangle \(ABC\) is 100, find the area of the square \(CO_1PO_2\).

Given a triangle \(ABC\), a circle \(\Gamma\) through \(B\) and \(C\) with center \(O\) intersects \(AC\) and \(AB\) at points \(D\) and \(E\) respectively. Let the intersection of \(BD\) and \(CE\) be \(F\). Extend \(OF\) to intersect the circumcircle of \(\triangle ABC\) at \(P\). Let \(I_1\) and \(I_2\) be the incenters of triangles \(PBD\) and \(PCE\) respectively. If \(I_1I_2\) intersects \(BC\) at \(G\), find the ratio \(\frac{BG}{GC}\).

Among the following conclusions: \\
(1) The function $y= \sqrt {x^{2}}$ and $y=( \sqrt {x})^{2}$ are the same function; \\
(2) If the domain of the function $f(x-1)$ is $[1,2]$, then the domain of the function $f(3x^{2})$ is $\left[0, \frac { \sqrt {3}}{3}\right]$; \\
(3) The increasing interval of the function $y=\log _{2}(x^{2}+2x-3)$ is $(-1,+\infty)$; \\
The number of correct conclusions is ______.
Let $a \in \mathbb{Z}$, and $0 \leq a < 13$. If $51^{2016} + a$ is divisible by 13, then $a = \_\_\_\_\_\_$.
A rectangular field is one-third as wide as it is long, and it is completely enclosed by 72 meters of fencing. What is the number of square meters in the area of the field?

In triangle \(ABC\), let \(O\) and \(I\) be the circumcenter and incenter, respectively. \(AI\) intersects the circumcircle \((O)\) and \(BC\) at points \(S\) and \(T\), respectively. \(K\) and \(L\) are the incenters of triangles \(SBT\) and \(SCT\), respectively. Let \(P\) be the reflection of \(I\) through line \(KL\). If \(D\) is the midpoint of arc \(BC\) not containing \(A\), calculate the value of \(\angle BPD\) in degrees.

For \(a, b, c > 0\), find the value of \(m\) such that
\[
\frac{a^{m+2}}{b^m} + \frac{b^{m+2}}{c^m} + \frac{c^{m+2}}{a^m} \geq \frac{1}{3} \left( \frac{ab}{c} + \frac{bc}{a} + \frac{ca}{b} \right)^2.
\]
what is the minimum possible range in scores of the 3 test - takers ? 3 people each took 5 tests . if the ranges of their scores in the 5 practice tests were 18 , 26 and 32 .

Jimmy's father receives 20 emails a day. Halfway through April, he subscribed to a news channel that sent 5 more emails per day to his email. What's the total number of emails Jimmy's father had at the end of the month?

A, B, and C invested Rs. 6300, Rs. 4200, and Rs. 10500 respectively, in a partnership business. After a year, they made a profit, and A's share in the profit was Rs. 3750. What was the total profit made by the partnership business?
If the function $f(x)={2^x}-a⋅{({\frac{1}{2}})^x}$ is an even function, then $a=\_\_\_\_\_\_$, and the minimum value of $f\left(x\right)$ is ______.

Let $a_n$ be the number of permutations $(x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n)$ of the numbers $(1,2,\dots, n)$ such that the $n$ ratios $\frac{x_k}{k}$ for $1\le k\le n$ are all distinct. Find the remainder when $a_{10}$ is divided by $1000$.

Let \(ABC\) be a triangle and \(P\) be a point in the plane. Let \(A_1B_1C_1\) be the anticevian triangle of \(P\) with respect to \(ABC\). Let the radical axis of \(\odot (A_1PB_1)\) and \(\odot (ABC)\) meet \(AB\) at \(C_0\). Define \(A_0\) and \(B_0\) similarly. If \(A_0\), \(B_0\), and \(C_0\) are collinear, find the value of \(\frac{A_0B_0}{B_0C_0}\) when \(P\) is the circumcenter of \(\triangle ABC\).
You are trying to create two-digit numbers with 2, 3, and 7 allowing duplicates. Find the sum of all possible numbers.

the average monthly salary of 20 employees in an organisation is rs . 1500 . if the manager ' s salary is added , then the average salary increases by rs . 150 . what is the manager ' s monthly salary ?

Let $\{a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n\}$ and $\{b_1, b_2, \ldots, b_n\}$ be complete residue systems modulo $n$, such that $\{a_1b_1, a_2b_2, \ldots, a_nb_n\}$ is also a complete residue system modulo $n$. Find the sum of all possible values of $n$.
Given that the graph of the function $f(x)$ is symmetric to the graph of function $g(x) = \log_{\frac{1}{2}} x$ about the line $y=x$, find the value of $f(-2)$.
The number of positive integer solutions to the equation $x+y+z=12$ is ____.
When we should multiply a certain number by 16 and add 8, we mistakenly divide it by 16, and the quotient is 8 and the remainder is 4. Find the correct calculated value.

In triangle $ABC$, let the sides opposite angles $A$, $B$, and $C$ be $a$, $b$, and $c$ respectively. It is known that $a^{2}+c^{2}-b^{2}=ac$ and $\sqrt{2}b= \sqrt{3}c$.
$(1)$ Find the measure of angle $A$.
$(2)$ Let $f(x)=1+\cos(2x+B)-\cos(2x)$. Find the maximum value of the function $f(x)$.

In the polar coordinate system, the polar coordinates of two points $A$ and $B$ are given as $\left( 3, \frac{\pi}{3} \right)$ and $\left( 4, \frac{\pi}{6} \right)$, respectively. Calculate the area of $\triangle AOB$, where $O$ is the pole.
How many different number triangles are there with six consecutive numbers in the bottom line (in some order) and a top number of 2006?

A cricket player has played 10 innings with an average of 32 runs. He needs to make 76 runs in his next innings to increase his average of runs by a certain amount. By how much does he want to increase his average of runs per innings?

In a chess tournament with more than one male and more than one female participant, each pair of contestants played exactly one game with no ties. It is known that for every participant, the number of male participants they beat is the same as the number of female participants they beat. Determine the minimum number of participants in the tournament.
Sam found 200 seashells on the beach. He gave Joan 43 seashells, then gave Ali 27 seashells, and finally gave Lee 59 seashells. He has _____ many seashells now.
A soccer league consists of ten teams. During the league, each team plays exactly two games with each of the other teams. Calculate the total number of games played in the season.
Find the area of a trapezium whose parallel sides are 20 cm and 18 cm long, and the distance between them is 13 cm. What is the area of the trapezium?

Given an arithmetic sequence $\{a_{n}\}$ with the sum of the first $n$ terms as $S_{n}$, $a_{3}+a_{6}=a_{5}+4$, $a_{2}$, $a_{4}$, $2a_{4}$ form a geometric sequence.
$(1)$ Find the general formula for $\{a_{n}\}$ and $S_{n}$;
$(2)$ Let the sequence $\left\{{\frac{{50}}{{{S_n}}}}\right\}$ have a sum of the first $n$ terms as $T_{n}$, find the number of elements in the set $\{m|T_{m}=100-a_{k}$, $k\in N_{+}$, $m\in N_{+}$, and $k\geqslant 10\}$.
Given that \( x, y, z \in \mathbb{R}_{+} \), and \( s = \sqrt{x+2} + \sqrt{y+5} + \sqrt{z+10} \), \( t = \sqrt{x+1} + \sqrt{y+1} + \sqrt{z+1} \), find the minimum value of \( s^{2} - t^{2} \).
A digit was removed from a five-digit number, and the resulting four-digit number was added to the original number. The sum turned out to be 54321. Find the original number.
How many even three-digit integers have the property that their digits, read left to right, are in strictly decreasing order?

Rectangle $JKLM$ has sides $\overline{JK}$ of length 5 and $\overline{LM}$ of length 12. Divide $\overline{JK}$ into 200 congruent segments with points $J=P_0, P_1, \ldots, P_{200}=K$, and divide $\overline{LM}$ into 200 congruent segments with points $L=Q_0, Q_1, \ldots, Q_{200}=M$. For $1 \le k \le 199$, draw the segments $\overline{P_kQ_k}$. Repeat this construction on the sides $\overline{JL}$ and $\overline{KM}$, and then draw the diagonal $\overline{JM}$. Determine the sum of the lengths of the 399 parallel segments drawn.
Our club has 24 members, 12 boys and 12 girls. In how many ways can we choose a president and a vice-president if they must be of the same gender? Assume no one can hold both offices.
A piece of wire 5 feet 4 inches long was divided into 4 equal parts. How long was each part in inches if 1 foot is equal to 12 inches?
In how many ways can the digits of $64,\!420$ be arranged to form a 5-digit number, considering that numbers cannot begin with 0?

On the radius \(AO\) of a circle with center \(O\), a point \(M\) is chosen. On one side of \(AO\) on the circle, points \(B\) and \(C\) are chosen such that \(\angle AMB = \angle OMC = \alpha\). Find the length of \(BC\) if the radius of the circle is 6 and \(\cos \alpha = \frac{2}{3}\).

Given a sequence $\{a_{n}\}$ where ${a}_{n}=log_{2}(\frac{n+2}{n+1})$. A positive integer $k$ is defined as "good" if the sum of the first $k$ terms of the sequence $\{a_{n}\}$ is a positive integer. Find the sum of all "good" numbers within the range $\left[1,2023\right]$.
Sakshi can do a piece of work in 10 days. Tanya is 25% more efficient than Sakshi. How many days does it take for Tanya to do the same piece of work?

Find the coefficient of $x^{70}$ in the expansion of
\[(x - 1)(x^2 - 2)(x^3 - 3) \dotsm (x^{11} - 11)(x^{12} - 12).\]
What integer is closest to the value of $\sqrt[4]{15^4 + 10^4}$?
If the graph of the line \( y = ax + b \) passes through the points \( (3,1) \) and \( (7,13) \), what is \( a - b \)?

Let \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\) be positive numbers. Find the maximum value of the expression:
\[ \left( \frac{a}{a+b} + \frac{b}{b+c} + \frac{c}{c+a} - 1 \right) \cdot \frac{2(a+b+c)^3}{27abc} \]
Given an isosceles triangle $ABC$ with two sides of lengths 2 and 5, find the length of the third side.

Let \(ABCD\) be a cyclic quadrilateral with diagonals \(AC\) and \(BD\) intersecting at \(E\). Given that \(AE = 3CE\) and \(\angle BAD = 60^\circ\), calculate the value of \(\frac{AB + CD}{BC + AD}\).

Ellen is in charge of parking at a golf tournament. She must transport patrons from the overflow lot up to the main lot using a golf cart that can fit 3 patrons. There are 12 patrons who came in cars and some from a bus waiting in the overflow parking lot. Ellen needs 13 golf carts to transport them. How many patrons came from a bus?
Find the smallest positive multiple of $1996$ such that the sum of its digits is $1996$.

For $d > 1$ and $0 < c \leq d^{1/4}$, let $I(c, d)$ be defined as
$$
I(c, d) = \frac{\int_{c / d ^{1 / 4}}^{1}(1-t^{4})^{\frac{d-1}{4}} dt}{\int_{0}^{1}(1-t^{4})^{\frac{d-1}{4}} dt}.
$$
Find the value of $I(1, 5) + I(2, 17)$.
Virginia starts with 96 eggs. Amy takes 3 away. How many eggs does Virginia end with?
A candy store has 6 boxes of chocolates. Each box has 500 pieces. How many pieces are there altogether in the boxes?

Let \( x, y, z > 0 \). Calculate the minimum value of the expression
\[
\sum_{cyc} \left( \frac{x^3}{(y+z)^3} - \frac{y^3 z^3}{(x^2 + yz)^3} \right).
\]

Megan has read some books this year. Kelcie has read 1/4 the amount of books that Megan has read. Greg has read 9 more than twice the number of books that Kelcie has read. Together, they have read a total of 65 books. How many books has Megan read?

On a school bus trip, 41 children were initially riding on the bus. At the first bus stop, 12 children got off while 5 got on. At the second bus stop, 7 children got off and 10 got on. At the third bus stop, 14 children got off and 3 got on. Finally, at the fourth bus stop, 9 children got off and 6 got on the bus. How many more children were on the bus before the first bus stop than at the final stop?

Let \(ABC\) be a triangle with circumcircle \(c\) and circumcenter \(O\), and let \(D\) be a point on the side \(BC\) different from the vertices and the midpoint of \(BC\). Let \(K\) be the point where the circumcircle \(c_1\) of the triangle \(BOD\) intersects \(c\) for the second time and let \(Z\) be the point where \(c_1\) meets the line \(AB\). Let \(M\) be the point where the circumcircle \(c_2\) of the triangle \(COD\) intersects \(c\) for the second time and let \(E\) be the point where \(c_2\) meets the line \(AC\). Finally, let \(N\) be the point where the circumcircle \(c_3\) of the triangle \(AEZ\) meets \(c\) again. Calculate the area of triangle \(NKM\) given that the area of triangle \(ABC\) is 120 square units.

Initially, the number 10 is written on the board. In each subsequent move, you can either:
(i) erase the number 1 and replace it with a 10, or 
(ii) erase the number 10 and replace it with a 1 and a 25, or 
(iii) erase a 25 and replace it with two 10. 
After some time, you notice that there are exactly one hundred copies of 1 on the board. What is the least possible sum of all the numbers on the board at that moment?
For real numbers \(a, b, c\), let \(f(a, b, c) = (a^2 - a + 1)(b^2 - b + 1)(c^2 - c + 1) - (2\sqrt{3} - 3)(a^2b^2c^2 - abc + 1)\). Find the minimum value of \(f(a, b, c)\).

Find the value of the expression
$$\sum\limits_{k=0}^{10}(-1)^{10-k}2^{2k}\dbinom{10+k+1}{2k+1}.$$

Given $\triangle ABC$ is not isosceles at $A$. Let $(O)$ and $(I)$ be the circumcircle and incircle of $\triangle ABC$, respectively. A rhombus has an area of 432 sq m, one diagonal has a certain length, and the other diagonal is 2400 cm. What is the length of the first diagonal?
Tom was at the beach for 5 days and found 7 seashells every day. Tom fond _____ seashells  during the beach trip .
If the complex number $z=(m^{2}-m)+mi$ is purely imaginary, then the value of the real number $m$ is ______.

Let \(ABC\) be a scalene triangle. Outside of this triangle, construct points \(B'\) and \(C'\) such that triangles \(ABB'\) and \(ACC'\) are congruent. Let \(D\) and \(E\) be points such that \(ABDC\) and \(AB'EC'\) are parallelograms. If the coordinates of \(A\), \(B\), and \(C\) are \((0,0)\), \((4,0)\), and \((1,3)\) respectively, find the \(x\)-coordinate of the point of concurrency of the lines \(BB'\), \(DE\), and \(CC'\).

Triangle  $ABC$  is right angled at  $A$ . The circle with center  $A$  and radius  $AB$  cuts  $BC$  and  $AC$  internally at  $D$  and  $E$  respectively. If  $BD = 20$  and  $DC = 16$ , determine  $AC^2$ .

In a certain animal shelter, the ratio of the number of dogs to the number of cats is 15 to some number. If 8 additional cats were to be taken in by the shelter, the ratio of the number of dogs to the number of cats would be 15 to 11. How many dogs are in the shelter?

A certain product's per-unit selling price $P$ (in yuan) over the past $30$ days is related to time $t$ (in days) with the function $p= \begin{cases} t+20,0 < t < 25,t\in\mathbb{N}^* \\ -t+70,25\leqslant t\leqslant 30,t\in\mathbb{N}^* \end{cases}$. The product's daily sales volume $Q$ (in units) is related to time $t$ (in days) with the function $Q=-t+40(0 < t\leqslant 30,t\in\mathbb{N}^*)$. Determine the maximum daily sales revenue for this product, and identify which of the $30$ days had the maximum daily sales revenue.

One side of an equilateral triangle of height $24$ lies on line $\ell.$ A circle of radius $12$ is tangent to $\ell$ and is externally tangent to the triangle. The area of the region exterior to the triangle and the circle and bounded by the triangle, the circle, and line $\ell$ can be written as $a\sqrt{b} - c\pi,$ where $a,$ $b,$ and $c$ are positive integers and $b$ is not divisible by the square of any prime. What is $a+b+c\,?$
The sum of two numbers is 50 and their difference is 16. What is the greater of the two numbers?

Given a [rational number](https://artofproblemsolving.com/wiki/index.php/Rational_number), write it as a [fraction](https://artofproblemsolving.com/wiki/index.php/Fraction) in lowest terms and calculate the product of the resulting [numerator](https://artofproblemsolving.com/wiki/index.php/Numerator) and [denominator](https://artofproblemsolving.com/wiki/index.php/Denominator). For how many rational numbers between $0$ and $1$ will $20_{}^{}!$ be the resulting [product](https://artofproblemsolving.com/wiki/index.php/Product)?

Given \(a_{1}+a_{2}+a_{3}+\ldots+a_{99}+a_{100}=0\). Find:

\(1 \cdot\left(a_{1}-a_{2}\right)+2\left(a_{2}-a_{3}\right)+3\left(a_{3}-a_{4}\right)+\ldots+99\left(a_{99}-a_{100}\right)+100 a_{100}\).

Two spheres with radii 36 and one sphere with radius 13 are each externally tangent to the other two spheres and to two different planes \(\mathcal{P}\) and \(\mathcal{Q}\). The intersection of planes \(\mathcal{P}\) and \(\mathcal{Q}\) is the line \(\ell\). The distance from line \(\ell\) to the point where the sphere with radius 13 is tangent to plane \(\mathcal{P}\) is \(\frac{m}{n}\), where \(m\) and \(n\) are relatively prime positive integers. Find \(m + n\).

Consider a sequence \(\{ x_n \}\) in \(l_2\). Let \(S\) be the set of sequences \(\{ y_n \} \in l^2\) such that \(|y_n| \leq |x_n|\) for all \(n = 1, 2, \ldots\). Given \(\epsilon = 0.01\), find the smallest integer \(N\) such that for any \(\{ y_n \} \in S\),

\[
\sum_{n=N}^{\infty} |y_n|^2 < \epsilon.
\]
On dividing a certain number by 164.98876404494382, we get 89 as quotient and 14 as remainder. What is the dividend?
Compute $2 + 8 \cdot 3 - 4 + 7 \cdot 2 \div 2$.

Calculate:
$$
10 \times 9 \times 8 + 7 \times 6 \times 5 + 6 \times 5 \times 4 + 3 \times 2 \times 1 - 9 \times 8 \times 7 - 8 \times 7 \times 6 - 5 \times 4 \times 3 - 4 \times 3 \times 2
$$
A quadrilateral has one angle measuring 120 degrees. How many obtuse angles can this quadrilateral have at maximum?
