\]

Given a geometric series \(\left\{a_{n}\right\}\) with the sum of its first \(n\) terms denoted by \(S_{n}\), and satisfying the equation \(S_{n}=\frac{\left(a_{n}+1\right)^{2}}{4}\), find the value of \(S_{20}\).

Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle with points $R$, $P$, and $Q$ on sides $AB$, $BC$, and $AC$ respectively. Let $r$, $r_1$, $r_2$, $r_3$, and $r_4$ be the inradii of triangles $\triangle ABC$, $\triangle AQR$, $\triangle BPR$, $\triangle CPQ$, and $\triangle RPQ$. If $r = 6$, calculate the maximum possible value of $r_1 + r_2 + r_3 + r_4$.

Given that the function \( f \) satisfies \( f(2+x) = f(2-x) \) for every real number \( x \) and that \( f(x) = 0 \) has exactly four distinct real roots. Find the sum of these four distinct real roots.

There are 50,000 employees working at a company. For each employee, the sum of the number of their direct managers and their direct subordinates is 7. On Monday, every employee issues an order and gives a copy of this order to each of their direct subordinates (if they have any). On the following days, every worker takes all the orders they received the previous day and either distributes copies of them to all their direct subordinates or, if they have none, carries out the orders themselves. It turns out that by Friday, no orders are being transmitted within the company. Prove that the company has at least 97 managers who have no managers above them.

Let $ a$, $ b$, $ c$, $ x$, $ y$, and $ z$ be real numbers satisfying:
\begin{align*}
  17x +  b y +  c z &= 0 \\
   a x + 29 y +  c z &= 0 \\
   a x +  b y + 53 z &= 0.
\end{align*}
Assume that $ a \ne 17$ and $ x \ne 0$. Find the value of:
\[ \frac{a}{a - 17} + \frac{b}{b - 29} + \frac{c}{c - 53} \, ?\]
Find the coefficient of $x^2$ when $4(x - x^3) - 3(x^2 - x^3 + x^5) + 2(4x^2 - x^9)$ is simplified.

A can complete a project in some days and B can complete the same project in 30 days. If A and B start working on the project together and A quits 10 days before the project is completed, the project will be completed in 18 days. In how many days can A complete the project alone?
Simplify $\sqrt{5\cdot 3}\cdot \sqrt{3^3\cdot 5^3}$.
The average score of a cricketer for 12 matches is 48 runs. If the average for the first 8 matches is 40, then what is the average for the last 4 matches?

Let \( p_{1}, p_{2}, \ldots, p_{97} \) be prime numbers (not necessarily distinct). What is the maximum integer value that the expression

$$
\sum_{i=1}^{97} \frac{p_{i}}{p_{i}^{2}+1}=\frac{p_{1}}{p_{1}^{2}+1}+\frac{p_{2}}{p_{2}^{2}+1}+\ldots+\frac{p_{97}}{p_{97}^{2}+1}
$$

can take?

A library has eight identical copies of a certain book. At any given time, some of these copies are at the library and some are checked out. How many different ways are there for some of the books to be in the library and the rest to be checked out if at least two books are in the library and at least two are checked out?

For every $m \geq 2$, let $Q(m)$ be the least positive integer with the following property: For every $n \geq Q(m)$, there is always a perfect cube $k^3$ in the range $n < k^3 \leq m \cdot n$. Find the remainder when $$\sum_{m = 2}^{2017} Q(m)$$ is divided by 1000.

Math City has now ten streets, none of which are parallel and no three streets meet at a single point. One police officer is stationed at each intersection. What is the greatest number of police officers needed?

Let \( f_0: \mathbb{Z} \rightarrow \mathbb{R} \) and for every \( t \in \mathbb{N} \), define

\[ f_{t+1}(n) = \frac{f_t(n-1) + f_t(n+1)}{2}. \]

Define for every function \( g \),

\[ V(g) = \sum_{-\infty \leq n \leq +\infty} |g(n+1) - g(n)|. \]

Define \( f^*(n) = \sup_t f_t(n) \). Suppose that \( V(f_0) < +\infty \). Calculate the value of \( V(f^*) \) if \( V(f_0) = 10 \).

A scientist used a unique four - color code to identify each of the test subjects involved in a certain study. If the scientist found that choosing from among 8 colors produced enough color codes to identify all but 19 of the test subjects, how many test subjects were in the study? (Assume that the order of the colors in the codes does not matter and each color can be used only once in a code.)

A drink vendor has 60 liters of Maaza, 144 liters of Pepsi and some liters of Sprite. He wants to pack them in cans, so that each can contains the same number of liters of a drink, and doesn't want to mix any two drinks in a can. The least number of cans required is 143. How many liters of Sprite does the vendor have?

Consider placing queens on a standard $8 \times 8$ chessboard such that each queen attacks exactly $n$ other queens, where $1 \leq n \leq 8$. For each value of $n$, determine the minimum number of queens required to achieve this configuration. Calculate the sum of these minimum numbers of queens for all values of $n$ from $1$ to $8$.
In △AOB, there are 4 points on edge OA and 5 points on edge OB, including point O, making a total of 10 points. The number of triangles formed by taking these 10 points as vertices is $\_\_\_\_\_\_$.

on thursday mabel handled 90 transactions . anthony handled 10 % more transactions than mabel , cal handled 2 / 3 rds of the transactions that anthony handled , and jade handled 17 more transactions than cal . how much transactions did jade handled ?
The sum of the first five terms of an arithmetic sequence is $15$. If the fourth term is $4$, what is the seventh term?

Given a hyperbola $C:\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1(a＞0,b＞0)$, one of its asymptotes is perpendicular to the line $x+2y=0$, and the distance from the right vertex $A$ to this asymptote is $\frac{2\sqrt{5}}{5}$.
$(1)$ Find the equation of the hyperbola $C$;
$(2)$ If the line $l$ intersects the hyperbola $C$ at points $A$ and $B$, with the midpoint of segment $AB$ at $M\left(3,2\right)$, find the slope of the line $l$.
A train crosses a platform in 36 sec while it crosses a signal pole in 18 sec. The length of the platform is 300 m. What is the length of the train?

Two points, $E$ and $F$, lie on the same side of line $XY$ such that $\triangle XEY$ and $\triangle XYF$ are congruent with $XY = 7$, $EY=FX=15$, and $EX=FY=13$. The intersection of these two triangular regions has area $\frac{p}{q}$, where $p$ and $q$ are relatively prime positive integers. Find $p+q$.

Let \(a, b, c\) be positive real numbers such that \(-1 < \lambda < \min \left\{\frac{b+c}{a}, \frac{c+a}{b}, \frac{a+b}{c}\right\}\). Calculate the maximum value of the expression:
\[
\frac{c-a}{b+c-\lambda a} + \frac{a-b}{c+a-\lambda b} + \frac{b-c}{a+b-\lambda c}.
\]

Let \( n \) be a positive integer and \(\{a_i, b_i\}(1 \leqslant i \leqslant n)\) are pairwise disjoint subsets of \(\{1, 2, \dots, 2n\}\). Define \( f: \{1, 2, \dots, 2n\} \rightarrow \{-1, 1\} \) such that \( f(a_i) + f(b_i) = 0 \) for all \( 1 \leqslant i \leqslant n \), and also 
\[
\left| \sum_{j=1}^{k} f(j) \right| \leqslant 1
\]
for all \( 1 \leqslant k \leqslant 2n \). Find the number of such functions \( f \) for \( n = 5 \).
Determine the sum of the possible values of $a$ if the zeroes of the function $f(x) = x^2 - ax + 3a$ are integers.

The circle given by the equation $2x^2 = -2y^2 + 16x - 8y + 40$ is inscribed inside a rectangle which has a pair of sides parallel to the x-axis. Find the area of the rectangle if the length of the rectangle is twice its width.
The first three terms of an arithmetic sequence are 3, 13, and 23, respectively. What is the sum of the first 21 terms?
What is the coefficient of the $x^3y^4$ term in the expansion of $(x+y)^7$?

Let \(ABC\) be a triangle with incenter \(I\), and let \(d_1, d_2\) be two perpendicular lines passing through \(I\). Define \(A_1, A_2\) as the projections of \(A\) onto \(d_1\) and \(d_2\), respectively, and similarly define \(B_1, B_2\) and \(C_1, C_2\). Let \(O'\) be the circumcenter of the triangle formed by the segments \(A_1A_2\), \(B_1B_2\), and \(C_1C_2\). If the nine-point circle of triangle \(ABC\) has a radius of \(R\), find the value of \(R^2 - IO'^2\).

The function \( f(x) \) satisfies for all real numbers \( x \):
\[ f(2-x) = f(2+x) \]
\[ f(5+x) = f(5-x) \]
and \( f(0) = 0 \).

Determine the minimum number of zeros of \( f(x) \) on the interval \([-21, 21]\).
Let \(a, b, c, d\) be positive integers such that \(abcd = a^2 + b^2 + c^2 + 1\). If \(a \leq b \leq c\), find the value of \(d\) when \(a = 1\), \(b = 2\), and \(c = 3\).

In triangle \( \triangle ABC \), the incircle \( k \) touches \( BC \) and \( CA \) at points \( P \) and \( Q \) respectively. Let \( J \) be the center of the excircle opposite to side \( AB \). Let \( T \) be the intersection of the circumcircles of \( \triangle JBP \) and \( \triangle JAQ \) other than \( J \). If \( R \) is the radius of the circumcircle of \( \triangle ABT \) and \( r \) is the radius of the incircle \( k \), find the value of \( \frac{R}{r} \) given that \( AB = 13 \), \( BC = 14 \), and \( CA = 15 \).
Let $g(x)$ be a polynomial with real, nonnegative coefficients.  If $g(5) = 20$, $g(20) = 800$, and $g(7) = 28$, find the largest possible value of $g(14)$.
In the sequence $\{a_n\}$, $a_{n+1} = 2a_n$. If $a_5 = 4$, then the value of $a_4a_5a_6$ is \_\_\_\_\_\_.
Find the least positive integer $x$ that satisfies $x + 7351 \equiv 3071 \pmod{17}$.
Some black cards were taken out from a deck of cards. There are 21 remaining black cards. How many black cards were taken out?

A stick 7 cm long, a stick 11 cm long, and a third stick $n$ cm long form a triangle. The perimeter of the triangle must be greater than 35 cm. What is the sum of all possible whole number values of $n$?

In triangle \( ABC \), \( \angle ABC = 90^\circ \) and \( AD \) is an angle bisector. Given \( AB = 100 \), \( BC = y \), and \( AC = 3y - 10 \), find the area of \( \triangle ADC \). Round your answer to the nearest integer.
The decimal expansion of $37^9$ is $129A617B979C077$ for digits $A, B,$ and $C$. Find the three-digit number $ABC$.
The function $f(x) = a\sin x + bx\cos x - 2c\tan x + x^2$, if $f(-2) = 3$, then $f(2) = \underline{\quad}$.
For a given positive integer \( n > 3^2 \), what is the greatest common divisor of \( n^4 + 4^2 \) and \( n + 3 \)?
How many obtuse interior angles are possible in a convex quadrilateral?
A certain solution of salt and water is 10% salt. To decrease the salt to 8% of the volume, 14 gallons of water must be added. What is the initial volume of the solution in gallons?
If a non-negative integer k exists such that 12^k is a divisor of 856,736, then 3^k - k^3 = 1. What is the value of k?
If the graph of the function $y=\left(a-1\right)x^{2}-4x+2a$ has exactly one point of intersection with the $x$-axis, then the value of $a$ is ____.
Evaluate the limit $$L=\lim_{x\to0} \left(\frac{\sum_{k=1}^n k^x}{n+1}\right)^{1/x}.$$

Petya and Vasya each brought the same number $N$ of sets of pastries for tea.

Each set contained either 3 or 5 pastries. When they each unpacked their pastries and placed them on a plate, it turned out that Petya brought a total of 25 pastries, and Vasya brought 35. Find the number $N$ of sets brought by each of the boys.

Triangle $ABC$ has positive integer side lengths with $AB=AC$. Let $I$ be the intersection of the bisectors of $\angle B$ and $\angle C$. Suppose $BI=8$. Find the smallest possible perimeter of $\triangle ABC$.

You start with a number. Every second, you can add or subtract any number of the form \( n! \) to your current number to get a new number. In how many ways can you get from 0 to 100 in 4 seconds? (\( n! \) is defined as \( n \times (n-1) \times (n-2) \times \cdots \times 2 \times 1 \), so \( 1! = 1, 2! = 2, 3! = 6, 4! = 24 \), etc.)

At Theo’s cafe, he makes some egg and 4 egg omelettes. His cafe is open from 7:00 a.m. to 11:00 a.m. In the first hour, 5 customers order the smaller omelettes. In the second hour, 7 customers order the 4 egg omelettes. In the third hour, 3 customers order the smaller omelettes. In the last hour, 8 customers order the 4 egg omelettes. Theo needs 84 eggs to make all the omelettes. How many eggs are in the smaller omelettes?
An architect built a house with a certain number of bedrooms. The second floor had two bedrooms and the first floor had 8 bedrooms. How many bedrooms does the house have in total?
How many integers between 20 and 120 are relatively prime to 24?
Megan had 40 homework problems. She finished 26 of them but still had 2 pages of problems to do. If each page has the same number of problems on it, how many problems are on each page?

Compute the number of real solutions $(x,y,z,w)$ to the system of equations:
\begin{align*}
x &= z - w + xz, \\ 
y &= w - x + yw, \\
z &= x - y + xz, \\
w &= y - z + yw.
\end{align*}
If (x + 3)^2 divided by a certain expression equals 2, and the difference between the two possible values of x is 14, what is the expression in terms of x?
Define $g(x) = 3$ for all real numbers $x$. What is the value of $g((x-1)^2)$?
Given non-negative real numbers \(a, b, c, d\) satisfying \(\sum ab + 2\sum abc + 3abcd = 1\), calculate the minimum value of \(\sum a - 2\sum ab\).

How many ways are there to divide a group of 8 friends among the basketball team, the soccer team, the track team, and the swimming team? (Each team could have anywhere from 0 to 8 friends. Assume the friends are distinguishable.)

In an increasing sequence of four positive integers, the first three terms form a geometric progression, the last three terms form an arithmetic progression, and the first and fourth terms differ by $36$. Find the sum of the four terms.

Consider an arbitrary simple \( n \)-sided polygon. Determine the value of \( n \) for which there exists a point \( O \) such that each side of the polygon subtends an angle of \( \frac{360^\circ}{n} \) at \( O \), and the polygon is regular. Find the smallest such \( n \) greater than 3.

In triangle \( \triangle ABC \), let \( H \) be the orthocenter, and \( P \) be a point on \( BC \). Points \( Q \) and \( R \) are defined such that \( PQ \perp CA \), \( QC \perp BC \), \( PR \perp BA \), and \( RC \perp BC \). If \( Q \), \( R \), and \( H \) are collinear, calculate the value of \( \frac{PH}{HR} \) when \( P \) is the midpoint of \( BC \).

Each student in group A has 28 walnuts, each student in group B has 30 walnuts, and each student in group C has 31 walnuts. The total number of walnuts in the three groups is 365. How many students are there in total in the three groups?

Consider a function \( s\colon \mathbb{Q} \rightarrow \{-1,1\} \) such that for distinct rational numbers \( x \) and \( y \) satisfying \( xy = 1 \) or \( x + y \in \{0,1\} \), we have \( s(x)s(y) = -1 \). Let \( S \) be the set of all rational numbers \( q \) for which \( s(q) = 1 \). Find the number of elements in the set \( S \cap \{1, -1, 0, \frac{1}{2}, 2\} \).

Dr. Math's four-digit house number $ABCD$ contains no zeroes and can be split into two different two-digit primes ``$AB$'' and ``$CD$'' where the digits $A$, $B$, $C$, and $D$ are not necessarily distinct. If each of the two-digit primes is less than 50, how many such house numbers are possible?

João wrote down all the powers of 2, 3, and 5 greater than 1 and less than 2017 on a sheet of paper. Then, he performed all possible products of two distinct numbers from that sheet and wrote them on another sheet of paper. What is the number of integers that João recorded on the second sheet?
How many positive integers \( n \) are there such that there are exactly 20 positive odd integers that are less than \( n \) and relatively prime with \( n \)?
The sum of the $x$-coordinates of the vertices of a triangle in the Cartesian plane equals $15$. Find the sum of the $x$-coordinates of the midpoints of the sides of the triangle.

For a point \( P \) inside triangle \( ABC \), let \( d \) be the minimum value among \( |PA|, |PB|, \) and \( |PC| \). Calculate the maximum possible value of the expression \( \frac{d + |PA| + |PB| + |PC|}{|AB| + |BC| + |CA|} \).

Sasha heard that planting trees helps to reduce the local temperature. For each tree planted, the temperature drops .1 degree. A tree costs $6 to plant. She got the local temperature to drop from a certain temperature to 78.2, and it cost her $108 to plant the trees. What was the initial local temperature?
For how many pairs of consecutive integers in $\{2000,2001,2002,\ldots,3000\}$ is no carrying required when the two integers are added?
Given that $a$ and $b$ are positive integers satisfying $\frac{1}{a} - \frac{1}{b} = \frac{1}{2018}$, find the number of all positive integer pairs $(a, b)$.

In a physical education class, students line up in five rows to do exercises. The class has more than 50 students, with three rows having the same number of students, and two rows each having one more student than the other three rows. What is the smallest possible class size for this physical education class?

When the three-digit integer $MMK$, where $M$ and $K$ are digits and $M = K + 1$, is multiplied by the one-digit integer $M$, the result is the four-digit integer $NPMK$. What is the greatest possible value of $NPMK$?
Calculate $3^6 - 1$ and check how many prime numbers it is divisible by. What is the sum of these prime numbers?
If the roots of \( x^{2} - 2x - R = 0 \) differ by 12, find the value of \( R \).

Let $O_1O_2$ intersect the circles $\omega_1$ and $\omega_2$ at points $X_1, X_2$ and $Y_1, Y_2$ respectively. Determine a point $Q$ such that $\angle X_1QY_1 = \angle X_2QY_2$. Let $P$ and $P'$ be the points where the internal and external bisectors of $\angle X_1QX_2$ meet the line $O_1O_2$. If $O_1O_2 = 10$ and $X_1X_2 = 6$, find the length of $PP'$.
A 480 m long train is running at a speed of 55 km/hr. It crossed a platform of a certain length in 71.99424046076314 seconds. What is the length of the platform?

In the biotechnology class of 2000, there were 73 graduates. 32 of the graduates found a job, 45 continued on to their second degree, and some did both. If only 9 people didn't do both, how many graduates did both?
What is the sum of the largest and smallest prime factors of 1260?

In a triangle \(ABC\), \(H\) is the orthocenter. The circumcircle of triangle \(AHB\) intersects the extended line \(AC\) at \(X\), and the circumcircle of triangle \(AHC\) intersects the extended line \(AB\) at \(Y\). The segments \(XH\) and \(YH\) intersect \(AB\) and \(AC\) at points \(P\) and \(Q\) respectively. Let \(D\), \(E\), and \(F\) be the feet of the altitudes from \(A\), \(B\), and \(C\) respectively. If \(S\) and \(T\) are the points of intersection of \(EF\) with \(AB\) and \(DF\) with \(AC\) respectively, find the ratio \(\frac{ST}{PQ}\).

A large rectangle consists of three identical squares and three identical small rectangles. The perimeter of a square is 24, and the perimeter of a small rectangle is 16. What is the perimeter of the large rectangle?

The perimeter of a figure is the sum of the lengths of all its sides.

There are five students: A, B, C, D, and E.

1. In how many different ways can they line up in a row such that A and B must be adjacent, and C and D cannot be adjacent?
2. In how many different ways can these five students be distributed into three classes, with each class having at least one student?

If \(x\), \(y\), and \(z\) are positive numbers satisfying:
\[
x + \frac{1}{y} = 5, \quad y + \frac{1}{z} = 2, \quad z + \frac{1}{x} = 3,
\]
find the value of \(xyz\).
The constant term in the expansion of $$( \sqrt {2x}+ \frac {1}{x^{2}})^{n}$$ is \_\_\_\_\_\_ ．
What is the 150th digit to the right of the decimal point in the decimal representation of $\frac{17}{70}$?
Baker made 155 cakes. If his friend bought 140 cakes from him. How many cakes would baker still have?

On the squares of an $n \times n$ chessboard, there are hedgehogs on each square. Every second, the hedgehogs move to an adjacent diagonal square. What is the minimum number of squares that are occupied at all times?

On a $10 \times 10$ chessboard, there are $k$ grasshoppers, each moving in one of the four possible directions (parallel to the sides of the board). Each grasshopper jumps one square per second and reverses direction upon reaching the edge of the board. Determine the maximum value of $k$ such that no two grasshoppers ever land on the same square.
Find the value of the expression ( some x + 5 y ) / ( x - 2 y ) when x / 2 y = 3 / 2. The value of the expression is 26. What is the coefficient of x in the numerator?
smita was making a cube with dimensions 5 * 5 * 5 using 1 * 1 * 1 cubes . what is the number of cubes needed to make a hollow cube looking of the same shape ?

Let \( G \) be a finite group and \( \mathbb{Q}[G] \) be a group ring. Consider \( \mathbb{Q} \) as a \( \mathbb{Q}[G] \)-module with the action defined by:
\[
(a_1g_1 + \ldots + a_n g_n) \cdot a = (a_1 + \ldots + a_n) a
\]
Determine the rank of the free \( \mathbb{Q}[G] \)-module \( P \) such that \( P \) is projective and there exists a \( \mathbb{Q}[G] \)-module \( Q \) for which \( P \oplus Q \cong \mathbb{Q}[G]^r \) for some positive integer \( r \).

Let \(x, y, z\) be the side lengths of a triangle. Find the best constant \(k\) for which the inequality
\[
(x+y+z) \left(\frac{1}{x}+\frac{1}{y}+\frac{1}{z} \right) \ge 6 \left(\frac{x}{y+z}+\frac{y}{z+x}+\frac{z}{x+y} \right) + \frac{k(x-y)^2(y-z)^2(z-x)^2}{xyz(x+y)(y+z)(z+x)}
\]
holds.

The average (arithmetic mean) of all scores on a certain algebra test was 90. If the average of the 8 male students' grades was 87, and the average of the female students' grades was 92, how many female students took the test?
This pattern is made from matchsticks. If the pattern is continued by adding three matchsticks to the previous stage, how many matchsticks are used to create the figure for the $20^{th}$ stage?

Consider a function \( f: \mathbb{Z}^+ \rightarrow \mathbb{Z}^+ \) which satisfies the following conditions:
- If \( \gcd(m, n) = 1 \), then \( \gcd(f(m), f(n)) = 1 \).
- \( n \leq f(n) \leq n + 2023 \) for all \( n \in \mathbb{Z}^+ \).

Let \( S \) be the set of all prime numbers \( p \) such that there exists a positive integer \( n \) with \( p \mid f(n) \) and \( p \nmid n \). Find the sum of the elements in \( S \).
Alyssa had 7 puppies, and each of them had 4 puppies of their own. She then gave 15 of those puppies to her friends. She is left with _____ puppies.

the average score in an examination of 10 students of a class is 60 . if the scores of the top 5 students are not considered , the average score of the remaining students falls by 5 . the pass mark was 40 and the maximum mark was 100 . it is also known that none of the students failed . if each of the top 5 scorers had distinct integral scores , the maximum possible score of the topper is . . . . . .
Given the function $f(x)=\tan x+\sin x+2015$, if $f(m)=2$, then $f(-m)=$ \_\_\_\_\_\_.

Let \( g(x) = ax^2 + bx + 1 \in \mathbb{Z}[x] \) and \( f(x) = (x - a_1)(x - a_2) \cdots (x - a_n) \) with \( n \geq 7 \) and \( a_i \in \mathbb{Z} \) being pairwise distinct. Suppose \( g(x) \) is irreducible in \( \mathbb{Q}[x] \). Calculate the smallest possible value of \( n \) such that \( g(f(x)) \) is guaranteed to be irreducible in \( \mathbb{Q}[x] \).
Two numbers $120$ and $n$ share exactly four positive divisors. What is the second greatest of these four common divisors?
Jackson is buying chairs for his restaurant. He has 6 tables with 4 seats and 12 tables with 6 seats. How many chairs total does Jackson need to buy?

There are 800 points on a circle labeled clockwise as $1, 2, \cdots, 800$. They divide the circumference into 800 gaps. One point is selected and painted red. Then, the remaining points are painted red one by one according to the following rule: If the $k$-th point is painted red, then moving clockwise by $k$ gaps, the point reached is also painted red. What is the maximum number of red points that can be obtained on the circle? Provide a proof for your conclusion.

Max fills up water balloons for 30 minutes at a rate of 2 water balloons every minute. Max’s friend Zach fills up water balloons for 40 minutes at a rate of 3 water balloons every minute. In the process, some of the water balloons pop on the ground. Max and Zach have 170 filled water balloons in total. How many water balloons popped on the ground?

In a basket, there are 38 apples: 9 green, 12 yellow, and 17 red. Alyona sequentially takes apples out of the basket one by one. If at any point she has taken out fewer green apples than yellow ones, and fewer yellow ones than red, she will stop taking more apples from the basket.

(a) What is the maximum number of yellow apples Alyona can take out of the basket?

(b) What is the maximum number of apples Alyona can take out of the basket?

Gwen had 18 math problems, 11 science problems, 15 history questions, and 7 English questions for homework. If she finished 12 math problems, 6 science problems, 10 history questions, and 4 English questions at school, how many problems/questions did she have left to do for homework?
Evaluate $\lfloor (15.3)^2 \rfloor - \lfloor 15.3 \rfloor \cdot \lfloor 15.3 \rfloor + 5.$

A $17 \times 17$ table is colored in black and white arbitrarily. In every move, we choose an $m \times n$ table which is included in the square and switch all of its colors (including the inside). What is the minimal number of moves such that, in the end of the process, we can promise that the whole square is colored in white?

A tripod has three legs, two of which are each 6 feet long and the third is initially 6 feet long before the lower 2 feet of it break off. When the tripod is fully extended with unbroken legs, it forms an isosceles triangle at the base with the two longer legs, and the top of the tripod is 5 feet above the ground. After the break, calculate the new height, $h$, of the tripod's top from the ground. Express $h$ in the form $\frac{m}{\sqrt{n}}$, where $m$ and $n$ are positive integers with $n$ not divisible by the square of any prime. Find $\lfloor m + \sqrt{n} \rfloor$.
Given real numbers $a$, $b$, $c$ satisfying $a+b+c=0$ and $a^2+b^2+c^2=6$, find the maximum value of $a$.

Ella has $n$ containers of cookies, each container holding $15$ cookies. After eating two cookies, Ella is able to repackage the remaining cookies into parcels so that each parcel contains $11$ cookies without any leftovers. What is the smallest possible value of $n$?
If $300\%$ of $x$ is equal to $75\%$ of $y$, and $x + z = 24$ where $z = 8$, what is the value of $y$?
What is the least positive integer value of $x$ such that $(2x)^2 + 2\cdot 37\cdot 2x + 37^2$ is a multiple of 47?
a is some years older than b who is twice as old as c. The total of the ages of a, b, and c is 17. b is 6 years old. How many years older is a than b?
in an election between the two candidates , the candidates who gets 70 % of votes polled is winned by 280 vote ’ s majority . what is the total number of votes polled ?

Given three sets of integers \(a_1, a_2, \dots, a_7\); \(b_1, b_2, \dots, b_7\); \(c_1, c_2, \dots, c_7\), find the smallest possible value of \(k\) such that there exists a non-empty subset \(S \subseteq \{1,2,3,4,5,6,7\}\) with \(|S| = k\) satisfying \(\sum_{i \in S} a_i \equiv \sum_{i \in S} b_i \equiv \sum_{i \in S} c_i \equiv 0 \pmod{3}\).

Let \( f \) be a differentiable and non-constant function on the interval \([0,1]\) such that \( f(0) = 0 \). Define \( g(x) = e^{-x} f(x) \). Find the value of \( g(c) \) for some \( c \in [0,1] \) where \( g'(c) = 0 \).
The constant term in the expansion of $(x^{2}+2)( \frac {1}{x^{2}}-1)^{5}$ is $\boxed{\text{answer}}$.

Let triangle  $ABC$  be a right triangle in the xy-plane with a right angle at  $C$ . Given that the length of the hypotenuse  $AB$  is 60, and that the medians through  $A$  and  $B$  lie along the lines  $y=x+3$  and  $y=2x+4$  respectively, find the area of triangle  $ABC$ .
Find the value of $\tan^2\left(\frac{\pi}{7}\right) + \tan^2\left(\frac{3\pi}{7}\right) + \tan^2\left(\frac{5\pi}{7}\right)$.

Mary's sheep can run 12 feet per second, and her sheepdog can run 20 feet per second. A sheep standing a certain distance away from the sheep dog bolts, and the dog runs after it. It takes the dog 20 seconds to catch the sheep. How far away was the sheep from the sheepdog in feet?

Consider a set of \( n \) consecutive integers, where \( n > 2 \). For distinct positive integers \( i, j, k \) not greater than \( n \), find the smallest possible value of \( n \) such that there always exist distinct numbers \( i', j', k' \) in this set for which the product \( i'j'k' \) is divisible by the product \( ijk \).
The graph of the power function $f(x) = x^a$ passes through the point $\left(\frac{1}{2}, \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)$. Calculate $1 + \log_a f(4)$.
The greatest common divisor of 360 and 504 is ______.
Suppose a positive integer is expressed in base 8 as $CD_8$, and in base 6 as $DC_6$. Find this integer expressed in decimal.
Let $m$ and $p$ be positive integers with $p \ge 5$. Find the smallest positive integer $k$ such that $(mp)! \equiv m! \cdot p!^m \pmod{p^k}$ always holds.
I mistakenly subtracted a certain number from 954 instead of adding, and I got 468. Find out how much it is if you calculate it correctly.
If \( a \) and \( b \) are positive real numbers such that \( a \cdot 2^{b} = 8 \) and \( a^{b} = 2 \), compute \( a^{\log_{2} a} 2^{b^{2}} \).
If $P$ is a prime number and $P^2+2$ is also a prime number, then $P^4+1921=$ ?
Find the order of $1996$ in the sequence of positive integers consisting of only $1$s, $6$s, and $9$s in ascending order.

Jack and Jill went up the hill to fetch water to fill a 600 gallon tank. Each bucket is five gallons. Jack is stronger, and is able to carry two buckets of water at a time, but Jill can only manage one. Jack can complete a certain number of trips to the well and back in the time it takes Jill to make two trips. Jill made 30 trips before the tank was filled. How many trips can Jack make in the time it takes Jill to make two trips?

On a similarly labeled chessboard of $64$ squares, a man places $3^k$ grains of rice on each square $k$. How many more grains of rice are placed on the $8^{th}$ square than on the first $5$ squares combined?
How many zeroes does $15!$ end with, when $15!$ is written in base 12?

the average temperature for monday , tuesday , wednesday and thursday was 48 degrees and for tuesday , wednesday , thursday and friday was 46 degrees . if the temperature on monday was 43 degrees . find the temperature on friday ?

In triangle \( \triangle ABC \), let \( D \) be the foot of the \( A \)-altitude such that \( AD = BC \). Let \( M \) and \( N \) be the midpoints of \( BC \) and \( AD \) respectively, and let \( H \) be the orthocenter. Let \( l \) be the perpendicular bisector of \( BC \). If \( P \) is the intersection of \( MN \) with \( l \), find the value of \( \frac{MP}{PN} \).
He also needed some nails. If he already has 247 nails with him and he found another 144 in his toolshed, how many more nails does he need to buy if he needs a total of 500 nails?

Alice placed 3 cards on a table, each with one number visible and one number hidden. The numbers visible are 30, 42, and 36. It is known that the sums of the numbers on each card are equal and that the numbers on the hidden sides are consecutive odd numbers. What is the average of the hidden numbers?

Let \( p_1 < p_2 < \ldots < p_{31} \) be a sequence of prime numbers such that \( 30 \mid (p_1 + p_2 + \ldots + p_{31}) \). Find the smallest possible value of \( p_{31} \) if the set \( S = \{ p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_{31} \} \) contains three consecutive prime numbers.

For the past n days, the average daily production at a company was 50 units. If today's production of 115 units raises the average to a certain number of units per day, and the value of n is 12, what is the new average daily production?
Find the maximum and minimum values of the function \( y = 3x^4 + 4x^3 + 34 \) on the interval \([-2, 1]\).

for all real \( b \geq 0 \). Calculate this minimum value for \( k = 3 \).

Given the function $f(x)=2\sin(2x-\frac{π}{6})$.

What is the total weight of the five new people?

Let \( P \) be a point outside the convex quadrilateral \( ABCD \) such that \( AD \) separates \( P \) and \( B \). Given that \([PAB] \cdot [PCD] = [PBC] \cdot [PAD]\), calculate the value of \(\frac{MA}{MN} \cdot \frac{DN}{DA}\).

Find all functions \( f: \mathbb{R}^+ \to \mathbb{R}^+ \) such that:

find the area of a parallelogram with base 12 cm and height 48 cm ?

In the floor of a particular kitchen owned by an abstract artist, each row of tiles to the right of the first row contains two fewer tiles than the row directly to its left. There are 9 rows in all and a total of 405 tiles in the floor. How many tiles does the leftmost row contain?

Let \(ABC\) be a triangle with Nagel cevians \(n_a, n_b, n_c\) from vertices \(A, B, C\) respectively, and let \(R\) and \(r\) denote the circumradius and inradius of the triangle. Convert $205_{10}$ into base 2. Let $u$ represent the number of zeros and $v$ the number of ones in the binary form. Calculate $2(v-u)$.

Let \(a, b, c \in [0,1]\). Find the minimum value of the expression

Consider a five-by-five square arrangement of dots. What is the smallest number of dots that need to be circled to ensure that each row, column, and diagonal of dots has at least 1 dot circled?

He also has to pay a weekly fee of $100. He has to pay $7800 in a year. How many miles does he drive on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday?

Denis threw darts at four identical dartboards: he threw exactly three darts at each board. The points he scored are shown in the image. On the first board, he scored 30 points, on the second board - 38 points, and on the third board - 41 points. How many points did he score on the fourth board? (Each specific zone - ring or central field - awards a certain number of points.)

Let \( a \), \( b \), and \( c \) be positive real numbers such that \( bc = 1 + a(b + c) \). Find the maximum value of the expression:
\[ P = \frac{6a}{\sqrt{1 + a^2}} + \frac{4}{\sqrt{1 + b^2}} + \frac{3}{\sqrt{1 + c^2}} \]
The decimal representation of a number is $0.\overline{27}$. When converted into a fraction and reduced to its lowest terms, what is the denominator of the fraction?
Find the value of the constant term in the binomial expansion of $(x+ \frac {1}{x})^{4}$.
Joshua initially has 150 bottle caps. He buys 23 more and decides to give away 37 of them to his friend. In all, Joshua has _____ bottle caps.

In a room with 2024 people, it is known that for every 4 people, at least one person is friends with the other 3. Let \( S \) be the set of people who are friends with every person in the room. Calculate the minimum possible size of \( S \).

Let a square have side length \( (x - 4) \), and a rectangle have length \( (2x - 6) \) and width \( (x + 2) \). If the area of the rectangle is triple the area of the square, what is the sum of all possible values of \( x \)?

The soccer team had him fill a certain number of bottles. The lacrosse team needed 12 more bottles than the football team. He filled 49 bottles for the rugby team during the final game he worked this season. How many bottles did he fill for the soccer team?

For each positive integer $n$, let $h(n)$ be the sum of the digits in the base-seven representation of $n$ and let $i(n)$ be the sum of the digits in the base-nine representation of $h(n)$. If $\angle GOH = 60^\circ$ and $GH = 600$, find the length of $BH$ expressed in the form $p + q\sqrt{r}$, where $p, q,$ and $r$ are integers, and $r$ is not divisible by the square of any prime. John had a stock of 1300 books in his bookshop. He sold 75 on Monday, 50 on Tuesday, some books on Wednesday, 78 on Thursday and 135 on Friday. The percentage of the books that were not sold is 69.07692307692308%. How many books did John sell on Wednesday?

In a sports complex, stations $A, B, C, D, E$ formed the vertices of a regular pentagon. These stations were connected by straight paths. Pat and Mat met at station $E$ and decided to sweep some of the paths. Pat swept the path from $E$ to $B$. Mat swept the path from $E$ to $A$ and also from $A$ to $F$.

Determine the difference in the lengths of the paths swept by Pat and Mat.
Find the sum of the vertices of a pentagonal prism and a hexagonal prism.
Find the units digit of \(n\) given that \(mn = 34^8\) and \(m\) has a units digit of 4.

Determine the smallest integer \( n \ge 2 \) such that \( B_n \) is divisible by 20, where \( B_n \) denotes the number of superb binary sequences with \( n \) terms. A binary sequence is called superb if each term is adjacent to at least one term that is equal to 1.

Let $w$ be a primitive root of an odd positive integer $n$. Let $r_1, r_2, \ldots, r_k$ be all positive integers $r$ such that $r < n$ and $\gcd(r, n) = 1$. Calculate the value of $(w^{r_1} + 1)(w^{r_2} + 1) \cdots (w^{r_k} + 1)$ for $n = 15$.

Let \( S \) be the set of integers that can be written in the form \( 50m + 3n \) where \( m \) and \( n \) are non-negative integers. For example, 3, 50, and 53 are all in \( S \). Find the sum of all positive integers not in \( S \).

Let $(G,\cdot)$ be a group with neutral element $e$, and let $H$ and $K$ be proper subgroups of $G$ such that $H \cap K = \{e\}$. It is known that $(G \setminus (H \cup K)) \cup \{e\}$ is closed under the operation of $G$. If $G$ has exactly 16 elements, find the number of possible distinct groups $G$ that satisfy these conditions.

Consider a polynomial $P(x,y)$ in the Cartesian plane. Let $S$ be the set of zeroes of $P(x,y)$. Define $f(n)$ to be the number of distinct geometric shapes (up to congruence) that can be formed by $S$ when the degree of $P(x,y)$ is $n$. Calculate $f(3)$.

Consider a quadrilateral \(ABCD\) with \(AB \cap CD = E\) and \(AD \cap BC = F\). Let the circles with diameters \(AC\), \(BD\), and \(EF\) intersect at points \(P\) and \(Q\). If the lengths of \(AC\), \(BD\), and \(EF\) are given by 10, 14, and 18 respectively, find the value of \(PQ^2\).

A math class has fewer than 50 students. When the students try to sit in rows of 8, 5 students sit in the last row. When the students try to sit in rows of 6, 3 students are left in the last row. How many students are in this class?

Let \(O\) be the circumcircle of triangle \(ABC\). The rays \(AO\) meet \(BC\) at \(A_1\) and meet the circumcircle again at \(A_2\). Similarly, we get points \(B_1, B_2, C_1, C_2\). Calculate the value of

\]

Let \( B \) be a subset of \( \mathbb{Z}_{3}^{n} \) such that for every two distinct members \( (a_{1},\ldots,a_{n}) \) and \( (b_{1},\ldots,b_{n}) \) of \( B \), there exists \( 1 \leq i \leq n \) such that \( a_{i} \equiv b_{i} + 1 \pmod{3} \). As shown in the figure, points \( A \) and \( A' \) are on the \( x \)-axis and are symmetrical about the \( y \)-axis. The line passing through point \( A' \) and perpendicular to the \( x \)-axis intersects the parabola \( y^2 = 2x \) at two points \( B \) and \( C \). The average height of 20 students in a class was calculated as 175 cm. It was later found that the height of one of the students in the class was incorrectly written as some cm whereas the actual height was 136 cm. The actual average height of the students in the class was 174.25 cm. What was the incorrectly written height of the student?

A natural number \( n \) is called interesting if \( 2n \) is a perfect square and \( 15n \) is a perfect cube. Find the smallest interesting number.

Say that a 4-digit positive integer is *mixed* if it has 4 distinct digits, its leftmost digit is neither the biggest nor the smallest of the 4 digits, and its rightmost digit is not the smallest of the 4 digits.  For example, 2013 is mixed.  How many 4-digit positive integers are mixed?

A broken calculator has the + and × keys switched. For how many ordered pairs \((a, b)\) of integers will it correctly calculate \(a + b\) using the labelled + key?

Peyton has some children and they each get a juice box in their lunch, 5 days a week. The school year is 25 weeks long. She will need 375 juice boxes for the entire school year for all of her children. How many children does Peyton have?
A and B go around a circular track of length 1200 m on a cycle at speeds of 36 kmph and 54 kmph. After how much time will they meet for the first time at the starting point?

For a given natural number $n \ge 2$, find the smallest possible value of $c$ among three distinct natural numbers $a, b, c$ between $n^2$ and $(n + 1)^2$ such that $a^2 + b^2$ is divisible by $c$. Calculate the sum of all such smallest possible values of $c$ for $n = 2, 3, 4, 5$.
Given positive numbers \( x \) and \( y \) such that \( 1 \leq x^2 - xy + y^2 \leq 2 \), find the minimum value of \( x^{6} + y^{6} \).
Mrs. Sheridan has 22 fish. Her sister gave her 47 more fish. How many fishes does she have now?

Let  $S = 1 + \frac{1}{\sqrt2}+ \frac{1}{\sqrt3}+\frac{1}{\sqrt4}+...+ \frac{1}{\sqrt{99}}+ \frac{1}{\sqrt{100}}$  . Find  $[S]$ .

You may use the fact that  $\sqrt{n} < \frac12 (\sqrt{n} +\sqrt{n+1}) <\sqrt{n+1}$  for all integers  $n \ge 1$ .

Half of the parrots on Bird Island are red, one-fourth are green, and the remainder are blue. Bird Island has recently welcomed 30 new parrots from Jungle Island, making the total count of parrots 150. How many of these parrots are blue?

The function  $g$  is defined about the natural numbers and satisfies the following conditions:  $g(2) = 1$  $g(2n) = g(n)$  $g(2n+1) = g(2n) +1.$ Where  $n$  is a natural number such that  $1 \leq n \leq 2002$ . 

Find the maximum value  $M$  of  $g(n).$  Also, calculate how many values of  $n$  satisfy the condition of  $g(n) = M.$

The program is as follows:  
t←1  
i←2  
while i≤4  
t←t×i  
i←i+1  
End While  
Print t  
What is the output of the above program?
What is the smallest positive integer $n$ such that $5n \equiv 789 \pmod{26}$?

Elvis is releasing a new album with 10 songs, but he doesn't want to waste too much time on writing. He spends 5 hours in the studio, where he writes, records, and edits his songs. Each song takes 12 minutes to record, then it takes 30 minutes to edit all of his songs.   How many minutes did it take Elvis to write each song, if each song took the same amount of time to write?
Annie likes to eat cookies. She ate 5 cookies on Monday, two times more on Tuesday, and 40% more on Wednesday than on Tuesday. How many cookies did Annie eat during these three days?

A relatively prime date is a date for which the number of the month and the number of the day are relatively prime. Determine how many relatively prime dates are in October, a month with 31 days where the month number is 10 (10 = 2 x 5).

Jack bought 55 apples. He wants to give 10 to his father and then equally share the remaining apples between him and some friends. Each of them will get 9 apples. How many friends will share the apples with Jack?

Consider the matrices 
\[ A = \left( \begin{array}{ccc} b & c & a \\ c & a & b \\ a & b & c \\ \end{array} \right), \quad B = \left( \begin{array}{ccc} c & a & b \\ a & b & c \\ b & c & a \\ \end{array} \right), \quad C = \left( \begin{array}{ccc} a & b & c \\ b & c & a \\ c & a & b \\ \end{array} \right). \]
Given that \(BC = CB\), find the sum of all possible values of \(a + b + c\) such that at least two eigenvalues of \(A\), \(B\), and \(C\) are zero.

Patricia is making a highlight film about her basketball team. She recorded video of every player and plans to put it all together in a longer movie. She has 130 seconds of the point guard, 145 seconds of the shooting guard, 85 seconds of the small forward, 60 seconds of the power forward, and some seconds of the center. On average, each player gets 2 minutes. How many seconds of the center does she have?
Evaluate $\left\lceil\sqrt{\frac{16}{9}}\right\rceil - \left\lceil\frac{16}{9}\right\rceil + \left\lceil\left(\frac{16}{9}\right)^2\right\rceil$.

Let $y$ be the largest positive integer such that $y$ divides $x^{1024} - x^{512}$ for every positive integer $x$. Find the sum of the not necessarily distinct primes in the prime factorization of $y$.
Compute $\dbinom{20}{19}$.

A necklace consists of 100 red beads and some number of blue beads. It is known that on any segment of the necklace containing 10 red beads, there are at least 7 blue beads. What is the minimum number of blue beads that can be in this necklace? (The beads in the necklace are arranged cyclically, meaning the last bead is adjacent to the first one.)

On the weekend, Tony will walk to the store at 2 MPH. On weekdays, he runs to the store at 10 MPH. The store is a certain distance away. If he goes on Sunday, Tuesday, and Thursday, the average time in minutes that he spends to get to the store is 56. How far is the store?

In the triangle shown, \( n \) is a positive integer, and \( \angle A < \angle B < \angle C \). The side lengths of the triangle are labeled as follows: \( AB = 2n + 10 \), \( AC = 3n - 6 \), \( BC = 2n + 16 \). Determine how many possible values of \( n \) there are.
For a given positive integer $n$, find the smallest possible value of $a + b + c$ for a triple $(a, b, c) \in \mathbb{N}^3$ satisfying the equation $a^2 + b^2 + c^2 = 3abc$, with $a, b, c > n$.

Two right triangles share a side such that the common side AB has a length of 8 units, and both triangles ABC and ABD have respective heights from A of 8 units each. Calculate the area of triangle ABE where E is the midpoint of side CD and CD is parallel to AB. Assume that side AC = side BC.

Let \( A_1 \ldots A_6 \) be a (possibly degenerate) hexagon with sides \( A_iA_{i+1} = a_i \) for \( i = 1, \ldots, 6 \) (where \( A_7 = A_1 \)). Assume that \( \sum_{1 \leq i < j \leq 6} a_i a_j = 15 \). Calculate the maximum value of \( \sum_{i=1}^{6} a_i^2 + 24 \cdot \prod_{i=1}^{6} a_i \).

A candy store wishes to mix 2 types of candy to get 5 pounds of 2 dollars per pound candy. If candy A costs 3.20 dollars per pound and candy B costs 1.70 dollars per pound, how many pounds of candy A should be mixed?
a farmer used 1,034 acres of land for beans , wheat , and corn in the ratio of 5 : 2 : 4 , respectively . how many y acres were used for corn ?

Given a sequence $\{a\_n\}$ with its sum of the first $n$ terms denoted as $S\_n$. For any $n ∈ ℕ^∗$, it is known that $S\_n = 2(a\_n - 1)$.

1. Find the general term formula for the sequence $\{a\_n\}$.
2. Insert $k$ numbers between $a\_k$ and $a_{k+1}$ to form an arithmetic sequence with a common difference $d$ such that $3 < d < 4$. Find the value of $k$ and the sum $T$ of all terms in this arithmetic sequence.
Find $n \in \mathbb{N}^*$ such that all natural numbers $m \leq \sqrt[3]{n}$ are divisors of $n$.
Given real numbers $x$ and $y$ satisfy $x^4 + x^2 = 3$, $y^4 - y^2 = 3$. Find the value of $x^4 + y^4$.
Three vertices of a cube are \(A=(3,7,4)\), \(B=(4,3,-5)\), and \(C=(7,-2,3)\). Determine the surface area of the cube.
A train 1500 meters long completely crosses a 1200 meters long bridge in 30 seconds. What is the speed of the train?
In an arithmetic sequence $\{a_n\}$ with a common difference greater than 1, it is known that $a_1^2=64$, and $a_2+a_3+a_{10}=36$. Find the sum of the first 20 terms of the sequence $\{|a_n|\}$.
For a given positive integer $k$, let $f(k)$ be the smallest positive integer $n$ such that there exists a prime $p > k$ for which $p^2 \mid 1! + 2! + \cdots + n!$. Find $f(5)$.
In a certain company, the ratio of male to female employees is 7 : 8. If 3 more men were hired, this ratio would increase to 8 : 9. How many male employees are there in the company currently?
Find the smallest positive integer $b$ for which $x^2 + bx + 1176$ factors into a product of two polynomials, each having integer coefficients.

Let \( m \) be the number of solutions in positive integers to the equation \( 4x + 3y + 2z = 2009 \), and let \( n \) be the number of solutions in positive integers to the equation \( 4x + 3y + 2z = 2000 \). Find the remainder when \( m - n \) is divided by 1000.
Renu can do a piece of work in some days, but with the help of her friend Suma, she can do it in 4 days. Suma can do it alone in 12 days. In how many days can Renu do the work alone?

Each letter of the alphabet is assigned a random integer value, with $H=8$. Calculate the values of words based on the sum of their assigned letter values. If $MATH = 32$ points, $TEAM = 40$ points, and $MEET = 36$ points, what is the value of $A$?

Ellen is baking bread. It takes 3 hours to rise 1 ball of dough, and then another 2 hours to bake it. If she makes 4 balls of dough one after another and then bakes them one after another when they're done rising, how many hours will it take?

In triangle $ABC$, $AB$ is congruent to $AC$, the measure of angle $ABC$ is $60^{\circ}$ and segment $BD$ bisects angle $ABC$ with point $D$ on side $AC$. If point $E$ is on side $BC$ such that segment $DE$ is parallel to side $AB$, and point $F$ is on side $AC$ such that segment $EF$ is parallel to segment $BD$, how many isosceles triangles are in the figure shown?

Lisa was collecting socks to donate to a homeless shelter. She bought 12 pairs at a discount store. Sandra, her friend, came over and brought her some pairs of socks. Her cousin showed up with one-fifth the number of pairs that Sandra bought. After work, Lisa’s mom brought 8 more than three times the number of pairs Lisa started with. How many pairs of socks did Sandra bring if Lisa ended up with 80 pairs of socks?

A rectangular farm has to be fenced one long side, one short side, and the diagonal. The cost of fencing is some amount per meter. The area of the farm is 1200 m², and the short side is 30 m long. The job would cost Rs. 1320. What is the cost of fencing per meter?

Joel selected an obtuse angle $x$ (strictly between 90 degrees and 180 degrees) and wrote the values of $\sin x$, $\cos x$, and $\tan x$ on three different cards. He then gave those cards to three students, Malvina, Paulina, and Georgina, one card to each, and asked them to figure out which trigonometric function (sin, cos, or tan) produced their cards. After sharing the values on their cards with each other, only Malvina was able to surely identify which function produced the value on her card. Compute the sum of all possible values that Joel wrote on Malvina's card.

In the updated game of Frood, dropping $n$ froods still gives a score of $\frac{n(n+1)}{2}$ points. However, eating $n$ froods now earns $15n$ points. What is the least number of froods for which dropping them will earn more points than eating them?
Let $n$ be the smallest positive integer such that $4021$ divides $2010! + n$. Find the remainder when $n$ is divided by $4021$.
If x is 30 percent more than y and y is some percent less than z, then x is 78 percent of z. What is the percentage by which y is less than z?

Several stones are placed in 5 piles. It is known that:
- The fifth pile has six times more stones than the third pile.
- The second pile has twice as many stones as the third and fifth piles combined.
- The first pile has three times fewer stones than the fifth pile and 10 fewer stones than the fourth pile.
- The fourth pile has half as many stones as the second pile.

How many stones are there in total across these five piles?

Let \( \triangle ABC \) be a triangle such that \( 0 < A, B, C < \frac{\pi}{2} \). Calculate the minimum value of the expression:
\[ \sin(2A)\tan B + \sin(2B)\tan C + \sin(2C)\tan A - \sin(2A) \sqrt{\tan B \tan C} - \sin(2B) \sqrt{\tan A \tan C} - \sin(2C) \sqrt{\tan A \tan B} \]

Let positive integers $a$ and $b$ be such that the product \[\log_a(a+2) \cdot \log_{a+2}(a+4) \dotsm \log_{b-4}(b-2) \cdot \log_{b-2}b\]
contains exactly $430$ terms, and its value is $3$. Compute $a+b$.

A hostel manager needs to label all rooms from 150 to 175 on one floor and from 250 to 275 on another floor. The room numbers require individual digits which are only sold in packages containing each digit from 0 to 9. How many packages must the manager purchase?
There are some children at a bakery. As they were deciding what to buy, 24 girls came in and 31 boys left. If there were 85 children at first, how many children were there in the bakery in the end?
For an entire month of April, Cora purchased 3 cookies each day. If each cookie costs 18 dollars. How much did Cora spend on cookies in April

Point $C$ is the midpoint of $\overline{AB}$, point $D$ is the midpoint of $\overline{AC}$, point $E$ is the midpoint of $\overline{AD}$, and point $F$ is the midpoint of $\overline{AE}$. If $AB=64$ units, what is the length of $\overline{AF}$ in units?
If 2023 were expressed as a sum of distinct powers of 2, what would be the least possible sum of the exponents of these powers?

A man walks around a circle of length 1 with an irrational step length 'a' (measured along the circumference). The circle has a ditch of width 'e' > 0. Let $N(e)$ be the smallest number of steps such that the man steps into the ditch, regardless of his starting position. If $e = \frac{1}{100}$, find the smallest integer value of $N(e)$.

The numbers from 1 to 217 are divided into two groups: one containing 10 numbers and the other containing 207 numbers. It turns out that the arithmetic means of the numbers in the two groups are equal. Find the sum of the numbers in the group of 10 numbers.

Given a triangle \(ABC\) with a circle \(\omega\) passing through vertices \(B\) and \(C\) and intersecting sides \(AB\) and \(AC\) at points \(R\) and \(S\) respectively. Let \(M\) be the midpoint of \(BC\). The line perpendicular to \(MA\) at \(A\) intersects \(BS\) and \(CR\) at points \(K\) and \(T\) respectively. If \(TA = AK\), find the value of \(\frac{MS}{MR}\).

Stacy bought two packs of printer paper for the office – one pack has 240 sheets, and the other has 320 sheets. Her office prints 60 one-page documents on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays, and 100 one-page documents on Tuesdays and Thursdays. Calculate the remaining printer paper sheets at the end of a two-week period.
In the Cartesian coordinate system $xOy$, the area of the closed figure formed by the line $x=a$ ($a>0$), the curve $y= \sqrt{x}$, and the x-axis is $\frac{2}{3}$. Find the value of $a$.

Let \(ABC\) be a triangle with \(H\) as its orthocenter and \(BH \cap AC \equiv D\). Let \(O\) be the circumcenter of \(\triangle ABH\) and \(M\) be the midpoint of \(AH\). Let \(OD \cap CM \equiv G\) and \(E \in AH\) such that \(CE \parallel HG\). If \(OD \perp DE\), find the value of \(\frac{DE}{OD}\).

On Monday, Jeremy (J) picks 100 oranges while at work on the farm. On Tuesday, together with his brother (B), they pick thrice as much as Jeremy did on Monday. Additionally, their cousin (C) joins them on Wednesday, and they now pick at twice the rate of oranges as they did on Tuesday.

On Thursday, Jeremy feels tired, and he picks only 70% of the oranges he picked on Monday, while his brother's performance remains consistent. Meanwhile, their cousin's performance varies according to weather conditions. On Wednesday, due to the overcast weather (W), the cousin picks 20% fewer oranges than the combined efforts of Jeremy and his brother on Tuesday. On Thursday, however, the sunny weather (S) allows the cousin to pick 30% more oranges than they picked on Wednesday.

With varying multipliers, variables, and weather conditions representing each individual's performance, determine the total number of oranges they picked over the four days.

One hundred fifty people were surveyed. Of these, $130$ indicated they liked Mozart and $120$ indicated they liked Bach. What is the minimum number of people surveyed who could have said they liked both Mozart and Bach?
The product of a number $N$ and eight less than $N$ is $7$. What is the sum of all possible values of $N$?

Given that the function $f(x) = x^2 + 2ax + 3$ is decreasing on $(-\infty, 1]$, and when $x \in [a+1, 1]$, the difference between the maximum and minimum values of $f(x)$ is denoted as $g(a)$. Find the minimum value of $g(a)$.

There are several positive numbers written on the board. The sum of the five largest numbers is 0.29 of the sum of all the numbers, and the sum of the five smallest numbers is 0.26 of the sum of all the numbers. How many numbers in total are written on the board?

A certain company in our city arranges 65 workers to produce two types of products, A and B. Each worker can produce 2 units of product A or 1 unit of product B per day. Through testing, it is found that the profit for each unit of product A is 15 yuan, and for each unit of product B is 120 yuan. However, in actual production, producing product B requires additional expenses. After calculation, it is found that for each unit of product B produced, the average profit per unit decreases by 2 yuan. Let x be the number of workers assigned to produce product B each day.

$(1)$ Fill in the table according to the information:

| Product Type | Number of Workers per Day | Daily Output (units) | Profit per Unit (yuan) |
|--------------|---------------------------|----------------------|------------------------|
| A            | $65-x$                    | ______               | $15$                   |
| B            | $x$                       | $x$                  | ______                 |

$(2)$ If the profit from producing product A per day is 650 yuan more than the profit from producing product B, what is the total profit the company can make per day by producing products A and B?

$(3)$ According to market demand, the company needs to increase the production of product C without increasing the number of workers. It is required that the daily output of products A and C be equal. It is known that each worker can produce 1 unit of product C per day (each worker can only produce one unit of product per day), and the profit for each unit of product C is 30 yuan. To ensure that the company can make the same profit as in question (2) when producing three types of products per day, how many workers should be assigned to produce product A?
For a geometric sequence $\{a_n\}$, the sum of the first $n$ terms is $S_n$. Given that $a_1=1$, and $a_1$, $S_2$, $5$ form an arithmetic sequence, then the common ratio $q=$ ______.

For Eeyore's birthday, Winnie-the-Pooh, Owl, and Piglet decided to give him balloons. Winnie-the-Pooh prepared three times as many balloons as Piglet, and Owl prepared four times as many balloons as Piglet. When Piglet was carrying his balloons, he hurried, tripped, and some of the balloons burst. Eeyore received a total of 60 balloons. How many balloons did Piglet end up giving?
In the sequence $\{a_n\}$, $(a_1=1, a_2=2)$, and $(a_{n+2} - a_n = 1 + (-1)^n (n \in \mathbb{N}^*))$, find the value of $(a_1 + a_2 + \dots + a_{51} = \_\_\_\_\_\_\_)$.
Given $x_{1}$ and $x_{2}$ are the two roots of the equation $2x^{2}-3x+1=0$, then the value of the algebraic expression $\frac{x_{1}+x_{2}}{1+x_{1}x_{2}}$ is ______.

Let \( p \) be a prime greater than or equal to 3. Let \(\{a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{p^2}\}\) and \(\{b_1, b_2, \ldots, b_{p^2}\}\) be two complete residue systems modulo \( p^2 \). Define \( S = \{a_{1}b_{1}, a_{2}b_{2}, \ldots, a_{p^2}b_{p^2}\} \). Find the smallest positive integer \( k \) such that \( k \) is not in \( S \) modulo \( p^2 \).

Twenty kilograms of cheese are on sale in a grocery store. Several customers are lined up to buy this cheese. After a while, having sold the demanded portion of cheese to the next customer, the salesgirl calculates the average weight of the portions of cheese already sold and declares the number of customers for whom there is exactly enough cheese if each customer will buy a portion of cheese of weight exactly equal to the average weight of the previous purchases. Could it happen that the salesgirl can declare, after each of the first  $10$  customers has made their purchase, that there just enough cheese for the next  $10$  customers? If so, how much cheese will be left in the store after the first  $10$  customers have made their purchases? (The average weight of a series of purchases is the total weight of the cheese sold divided by the number of purchases.)
Let \(a, b, c\) be positive real numbers. Find the minimum value of the expression \[\frac{a}{b} + \frac{b}{c} + \frac{c}{a} - 3 - \frac{29}{10}\left ( \frac{c-a}{c+a} \right )^2.\]
How many square units are in the area of a pentagon with sides of length 12, 17, 25, 18, and 17 units? The pentagon is arranged such that it can be divided into one rectangle and one triangle.

In triangle ABC, the angle bisector of angle ACB intersects the circumcircle of triangle ABC at point R and the angle bisectors of angles BCA and CAB at points P and Q, respectively. Let S and T be the midpoints of sides BC and CA, respectively. Calculate the ratio of the area of triangle RQT to the area of triangle RPS.
Let's say Julio is 42 years old, and James is 8 years old. In how many years will Julio's age be twice James' age?

Given an acute triangle \(ABC\), let \(A_1\) and \(A_2\) be points on segment \(BC\) such that \(BA_1 < BA_2 < BC\) and \(A_1A_2 = x = \text{constant}\). Similarly, let \(B_1\) and \(B_2\) be points on segment \(CA\) such that \(CB_1 < CB_2 < CA\) and \(B_1B_2 = y = \text{constant}\), and let \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) be points on segment \(AB\) such that \(AC_1 < AC_2 < AB\) and \(C_1C_2 = z = \text{constant}\). Let \((\alpha_1)\) and \((\alpha_2)\) be the circumcircles of \(\Delta AB_1C_1\) and \(\Delta AB_2C_2\), respectively, intersecting at \(A\) and \(A_0\).
